home_pitcher_note: Opening Day starts are nothing new to Hernandez, who will be making his eighth. Still, there will be some newness to the event. A 10-year Major League veteran, Hernandez will be making the shift to the AL for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: With Angels aces John Lackey and Kelvim Escobar out with injuries, Weaver emerged as the club's lead pitcher with a dominant spring, one that helped earn him his first Opening Day gig.

home_pitcher_note: Having shed 25 pounds during the offseason, Bonser is looking to prove that he can pitch deeper into games than he did in 2007. The right-hander suffered a bit of a setback in his sophomore season when he struggled to make it past the fifth or sixth innings of his starts. While his stamina hasn't really been tested yet, Bonser showed more life on his fastball and snap on his breaking pitches this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has been exactly what the Angels thought they were getting when they shipped Orlando Cabrera to the White Sox for him: a strike thrower who keeps his defense in the game and doesn't beat himself. He could be back in the form that made him a back-to-back 18-game winner in 2005 and 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Following an impressive stint in the Arizona Fall League, Blackburn emerged as not only a legitimate prospect in the Twins organization, but a true rotation candidate. A strong spring helped solidify Blackburn's spot.
away_pitcher_note: By his own assessment, Saunders had his best Spring Training. He has been in full command of his repertoire, which features a two-seam fastball that induces a lot of groundouts. He'll sneak a four-seamer past hitters on occasion.

home_pitcher_note: When the Twins sent Slowey down to the Minors last July, he was told to mix in all his pitches. The right-hander did just that in his September callup, posting a 3.34 ERA in six appearances that month.
away_pitcher_note: Which Santana will show up in 2008 -- the one who lost his spot in the rotation in '07, or the one who looked like a budding star in '06? The Angels are betting on the latter, convinced that Santana has corrected a flaw in his delivery.

home_pitcher_note: Once he got through the final barrier and was able to cut loose after off-season surgery on his ulnar nerve, Moseley showed that he has the right stuff to claim the fifth spot in the rotation with John Lackey sidelined by a strained right triceps. Moseley is a finesse pitcher who pounds the strike zone and relies on quality defense.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard was one of three players acquired from the Boston Red Sox on July 31 for reliever Eric Gagne. He was 2-1 with a 5.58 ERA in eight starts for the Rangers before being shut down in September because of soreness in his forearm. He has a 7.04 ERA in two career appearances against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: For openers, Weaver wasn?t razor-sharp, putting too many fastballs in good locations to Twins hitters. But he was resourceful in getting out of jams and kept his team in the game while yielding three earned runs on eight hits and two walks in 6 1/3 innings. His endurance (106 pitches) was excellent, and he struck out five hitters.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers are going with a four-man rotation for the first two weeks of the season because of two off-days and won't need a fifth starter until April 12. Luis Mendoza won that job when Brandon McCarthy went down with severe inflammation in his elbow. Saunders overcame some early-spring shoulder issues and a bout with food poisoning to fine-tune for his first Opening Day assignment. He was 1-0 with a 3.46 ERA in three Cactus League starts, getting most of his late work done in camp games, where he reached as high as 92 in his pitch count.

His two-seam fastball, curveball and changeup are his primary assets, but he can also bring the four-seamer up in the zone when the occasion calls for it. Catcher Mike Napoli refers to Saunders' "power changeup" as an out pitch, one the lefty can go to when he needs a strikeout as well as the four-seamer.

A bout with a kidney stone and several rocky outings in August cost him a shot at 20 wins. He was 5-2 after the break with a 3.94 ERA after taking a 12-5 record and 3.07 ERA to the All-Star Game.

away_pitcher_note: Braden, 25, has bounced back and forth between Oakland and Triple-A Sacramento over the past two seasons, getting called up to the A's nine different times. A 24th-round pick in the 2004 First-Year Player Draft, he was the Organizational Pitcher of the Year in 2005 and made his big league debut two years later. He won his first career start with Oakland but lost his next eight decisions and finished with a 6.72 ERA in 20 games -- the third-highest ERA in club history for a pitcher with more than 70 innings. In 2008 he was called up four times, making nine relief appearances before finishing the year with 10 consecutive starts. Shut down for the season on Sept. 11 with a strained groin, Braden posted a 3.97 ERA as a starter for the year and entered Spring Training as the team's projected No. 4 starter. After a string of strong outings early in Cactus League play and Duchscherer's injury, however, Braden was rewarded for following the coaching staff's orders to pound the strike zone and pitch to contact. Poised to make his first Opening Day start, Braden has a 2.25 career ERA against the Angels and went 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA in five appearances against them last season.

He was 3-0 with a 3.15 ERA in five Cactus League starts, with 15 strikeouts against only five walks in 20 innings. Moseley was 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three games against the Athletics last year and is 1-1 with a 7.57 ERA against the A's in seven career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, was Oakland's second-round pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft and in 2008 was named the A's Organizational Pitcher of the Year for the second consecutive season after leading the club's farm system with a 2.61 ERA while splitting the regular season between Single-A Stockton and Double-A Midland. Ranked by Baseball America as Oakland's No. 2 prospect and No. 11 in all of baseball, Cahill earned a spot in the starting rotation in his first trip to big league Spring Training. Having pitched in the 2008 All-Star Futures Game and in the Beijing Olympics as a member of Team USA, Cahill is no stranger to pitching under pressure, but he'll have to guard against overthrowing -- specifically, throwing so hard that the sink on his two-seam fastball disappears -- against the Halos. A Southern California native, Cahill will have several friends and family members in the stands for his coming-out party.

home_pitcher_note: Adenhart has been a different pitcher and person this spring, having matured at 22 with a more confident, assured presence on the mound. He had a superb spring and could be hard to ship down, if he maintains his stuff and confidence, when John Lackey, Kelvim Escobar and Ervin Santana return to claim their spots. He has all the tools: mid-90s fastball, 12-to-6 curve and a changeup that might be his best pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland, 25, is the most experienced starter in the Oakland rotation. Eveland made his big league debut in 2005 with the Brewers, who made him their 16th-round pick in the 2002 First-Year Player Draft.

Anderson, ranked by Baseball America as the top prospect in the A's organization and No. 7 in all of baseball, earned a spot in Oakland's rotation in his first trip to big league Spring Training, A 21-year-old who's drawn high praise from coaches and teammates for his poise on the mound, Anderson was a busy young man in 2008; he split the regular season at Single-A Stockton and Double-A Midland, pitched in the All-Star Futures Game at Yankee Stadium, played for Team USA in the Beijing Olympics, and finished the year on Triple-A Sacramento's playoff roster. away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start in six years, facing Ken Griffey Jr. in his return to Seattle in front of a packed home-opening crowd, Loux had a strong effort on Tuesday. He threw 110 pitches, which wasn't quite as efficient as his first start on April 10 against Texas, when he threw 97 pitches in seven innings, struck out eight, walked one and gave up one run on five hits.

away_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off an outstanding outing on Saturday against the Mariners in Seattle in which he went 7 2/3 innings, allowing no runs and five hits. Jackson allowed four runs over seven innings and took the win in his only start against the Angels last season.

away_pitcher_note: Bedard followed up the best outing of his Mariners career -- 8 1/3 innings of shutout ball in a 1-0 victory over the Oakland A's on April 12 -- with his second successive quality start in a loss to Detroit. Silva lost his only start against the Rays last year, going six innings and giving up four earned runs on eight hits, and hess 1-2 with a 2.84 against Tampa Bay in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver was impressive by showing his resiliency by lasting for seven strong innings despite allowing a run in each of the first three innings against the Tigers on Tuesday at Angel Stadium. away_pitcher_note: Washburn is off to his best start, by far, since joining the Mariners prior to the 2006 season. Now, the pressure is on Eaton to prove that he can get deep in the game on a regular basis.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders had his worst performance of the young season on Wednesday against the Tigers when he allowed five runs on seven hits over just five innings. Saunders struggled with his command and was removed after making 86 pitches through five innings. Saunders will happy to return to Baltimore, which is near where he grew up in Springfield, Virginia. home_pitcher_note: Uehara avenged his first career performance against Texas in his last start, pitching into the seventh inning and holding the high-octane Rangers to two runs. home_pitcher_note: One bad inning -- a four-run second featuring Jamie Hoffmann's three-run homer -- was Palmer's undoing against the Dodgers in a no-decision that ended his streak of five consecutive starts with wins. Palmer settled down after the early assault and lasted 4 2/3 innings, yielding four runs on five hits and two walks, striking out three. In his previous start, he'd picked up a win in Seattle despite giving up five earned runs across five innings. Fastball command backed by a quality breaking ball is Palmer's formula.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez threw 112 pitches against the Giants on Sunday, 83 for strikes, in his eight innings. He got ahead of the hitters, used all his pitches and worked both sides of the plate. He was victimized by an error that opened the door for three runs, all unearned. Now he faces a team that's a personal challenge. The last time he faced the Angels, May 19, they stole five bases. Manager Don Wakamatsu said afterward that he did not step up. But Sunday's effort should increase his confidence.

home_pitcher_note: Santana took a beating -- and so did his ERA -- when he surrendered seven earned runs while getting just three outs against the White Sox at home on Monday night in his third start of the season. He threw only 41 pitches in his brief outing, yielding a three-run homer to Jermaine Dye among the nine hits. Santana had a hard-luck loss to the Mariners in Seattle, yielding only one earned run in 6 2/3 innings, on May 20. He's 6-3 with a 3.76 ERA in 13 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Seattle manager Don Wakamatsu decided on Friday that Olson will start on Sunday against the Angels instead of right-hander Chris Jakubauskas, who was relegated to the bullpen after lasting just 3 1/3 innings in his last start. Olson pitched well against the Giants on Saturday when he threw six shutout innings, but he didn't figure in the decision. Olson is 1-1 with a 8.68 ERA in three career outings against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay gave the Jays seven solid innings in his last start, which came on Wednesday in Baltimore, but recorded a no-decision as the bullpen blew a five-run lead and Toronto lost 12-10 in 11 innings. Halladay gave up three runs in the outing -- all earned -- on eight hits and two walks, striking out five. He pounded the strike zone in typical Halladay fashion, throwing 74 of his 102 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders tossed 6 2/3 effective innings against the White Sox on Tuesday but pitched in and out of trouble all night. He ended both the third and fourth innings with strikeouts with a runner on third and loaded the bases in the sixth inning. But the damage was done with two solo home runs by Jayson Nix and a bases-loaded single by Paul Konerko in the sixth. In all, he allowed three runs on eight hits with four strikeouts and three walks. Saunders is 1-2 with a 3.62 ERA in four career starts against Blue Jays.
summary: 2009-06-02 - Los Angeles Angels (4) @ Toronto Blue Jays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Janssen earned his first win since May 24, 2007 on Friday. In his second start of the season, after missing all of 2008 with a shoulder injury and suffering a setback in Spring Training this year, Janssen went seven innings against the Red Sox at Rogers Centre, giving up three runs, all earned. He allowed 11 hits and two walks and struck out two. He threw 108 pitches -- 67 for strikes -- after tossing only 78 in his season debut, 50 of which were strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver was on top of his game again against the White Sox on Wednesday night, lasting eight innings and 103 pitches in holding Chicago to one run on four hits, walking two and striking out eight. Relying on fastball command, a quality breaking ball and an ever-improving changeup, Weaver struck out five of the first nine he faced. Few starters have been as consistent as the cross-firing right-hander, who yielded one or fewer runs in five of his past seven starts. He's 4-1 in five career outings against Toronto with a 3.38 ERA.
summary: 2009-06-03 - Los Angeles Angels (8) @ Toronto Blue Jays (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Tallet overcame some early problems with command and pitched seven innings against the Red Sox on Saturday at Rogers Centre, earning a win. He walked four batters in the first two innings and gave up three runs -- including a two-run homer by Boston right fielder Rocco Baldelli -- in those two frames. In the third through seventh innings, however, he allowed only two baserunners. He needed 59 pitches (29 strikes) to get through the first and second innings, but only 59 pitches (39 strikes) in the five innings that followed, bringing his pitch tally to a season-high 118. In total, he allowed three runs (all earned) on three hits and four walks, striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: The stamina was there, but Lackey wasn't as precise with his command as he needed to be while surrendering five earned runs on 10 hits in 7 1/3 innings against the Mariners on Friday night at home, absorbing his first loss in four starts since returning from a strained right forearm. Lackey reached 106 but struck out only two men while walking two, indicating his stuff was less than top shelf. He's 3-3 with a 3.39 ERA in 10 career starts against Toronto. At Rogers Centre he's 3-2 with a 3.11 ERA in seven outings.
summary: 2009-06-04 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Toronto Blue Jays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Verlander got a little roughed up in his last start, giving up nine hits in six innings -- including his first home run in more than a month -- and allowed three runs in the outing, as many as in his previous four combined. Yet he still earned the win, giving him a team-high six on the year, all of which have been in his last seven starts, and he continues to anchor the front of the Tigers' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Santana did not fare well in his last start, surrendering eight runs on 10 hits over just 5 1/3 innings against Seattle. He walked three, struck out two and watched his ERA soar to 9.50 following the start. Santana earned a no-decision in the outing though, as the Angels defeated the Mariners, 9-8.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson's career season is continuing in Detroit, where his 2.30 ERA is second in the American League behind Zack Greinke. His last outing may have been his best of the season: eight innings, two hits against the Orioles. And Jackson continues to be an "innings eater," as manager Jim Leyland calls him, going seven or more innings in four of his last five starts -- including his 132-pitch performance May 21 -- keeping the bullpen fresh for rookie Rick Porcello behind him in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday has been a long time coming for Escobar, who underwent right shoulder surgery last year. It will mark the first time he has pitched in a Major League game since Sept. 29, 2007, when he defeated Oakland for his career-high-setting 18th win of the season. In three Minor League rehab starts this year, Escobar has posted a 2.30 ERA across 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello descended from the stratosphere he occupied throughout May when he threw 4 1/3 innings, giving up seven hits and three earned runs in his last outing Tuesday. Before that, Porcello had won five straight starts, earning a 1.50 ERA over 30 innings. It wasn't a bad outing Tuesday, but Porcello said he struggled keeping the ball down in the zone, and he will look for better command of his sinker as he hopes to return to his previous form when he next takes the mound against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays in his last outing, Saunders endured a rocky start. The left-hander yielded six runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings. He picked up the loss, which was his second straight and third in four outings.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays continue to get solid outings from Shields, who plods along dependably and is one of the most underrated pitchers going in the league right now. His record doesn't do justice to how well he has been pitching, but Tampa Bay's offense finally bailed Shields out last Thursday. Shields went eight innings and retired 15 of the final 17 batters he faced but was in line for the loss until B.J. Upton hit a two-run home run in the eighth. Shields is 4-1 at home this season.
summary: 2009-06-09 - Los Angeles Angels (4) @ Tampa Bay Rays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It would be hard for Niemann to top his last performance. Frankly, it would be hard for any pitcher to top his last performance. Niemann took a perfect game into the fifth inning against the Royals and retired 12 of Niemann struck out a career-high nine batters, including the last batter of the game on his 100th pitch. Niemann has allowed only two runs over his past three starts, and the rookie has become an underrated asset as the Rays' No. 5 starter.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off the best of his five starts in his return from a right forearm strain. He held the Blue Jays to two earned runs across seven innings on June 4 in Toronto, striking out six while walking three and giving up seven hits. Finding his stamina with 114 pitches, Lackey has delivered three consecutive outings of at least seven innings, sliding quickly back into his role as the staff workhorse. He has dominated the Rays in his career, going 9-1 with a 2.36 ERA in 11 starts. The right-hander beat Tampa Bay in his only outing last year, going 7 1/3 innings. He is 2-1, 4.87 in three starts at the Trop.
summary: 2009-06-10 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ Tampa Bay Rays (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Price made his third start of the season on Saturday to take a no-decision against the Yankees. The 23-year-old left-hander went 5 2/3 innings against the Yankees and allowed just one earned run on two hits, leaving with a 5-3 lead that was lost by the bullpen. Price displayed electric stuff, but he continues to battle his pitch count. On Saturday, he threw 107 pitches -- of which just 53 were strikes, leading to five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's fifth start in his return from a sprained right elbow was what he and the Angels have been waiting for, a dominant effort. He was one strike away from his third career shutout when he yielded an RBI single to Magglio Ordonez, turning it over to Brian Fuentes for the final out against the Tigers at Comerica Park. Santana yielded six hits and two walks while striking out seven, mixing a quality slider and changeup with a fastball that was close to 2008 All-Star velocity. Santana is 3-3 with a 5.51 ERA in eight career outings against the Rays and is 1-3 with a 6.81 ERA at Tropicana Field in six starts.
summary: 2009-06-11 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ Tampa Bay Rays (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With Kelvim Escobar's shoulder not allowing him to start, Palmer is back in the rotation. He hasn't pitched since delivering seven scoreless innings in a May 30 no-decision against the Mariners, allowing four hits and no walks while striking out five hitters. Palmer has been much better at home -- he's 3-0 with a 3.18 ERA at Angel Stadium -- than on the road, where he's 2-0 with a 5.63 ERA. Making his 11th Major League start, Palmer will be sending his darting pitches at Padres hitters who haven't faced him.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin, coming off his best start with the Padres five days ago, when he allowed one earned run with no walks in 6 1/3 innings, didn't display that kind of command against the D-backs on Friday. He walked four and allowed a home run in the second inning to Chris Young, a solo shot that sailed over the wall in center field. He wouldn't allow another run until the fifth inning, when the D-backs struck for four runs. "I think I'm kind of crushing myself to make great pitches all of the time," Gaudin said. "With my last start in Colorado, I kind of took the approach to just put it in the strike zone and not worry about making the perfect pitch."
summary: 2009-06-12 - San Diego Padres (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Saunders struggled with his command early, giving up seven hits and three walks in his first three innings against the Tigers on Sunday in Detroit. He made it through six innings with four earned runs charged against him, stranding a total of eight runners. His fastball was live, but his breaking stuff was inconsistent. Saunders will be facing the Padres for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Jake Peavy was scheduled to make this start before being placed on the 15-day disabled list Friday with a right ankle injury. Geer allowed four runs in five innings in his last start, taking a no-decision against the D-backs.
summary: 2009-06-13 - San Diego Padres (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Despite having what he considered an off night in terms of "stuff," Weaver battled through five shutout innings Tuesday against the Rays and left having allowed only two runs in six innings. The issue was fastball command, but he compensated by keeping Rays hitters off-balance with a crisp breaking ball and an effective changeup. He has won five out of his past six decisions and has allowed more than one earned run in only five of his 12 starts this season. This is Weaver's first appearance against the Padres. He is 2-1 with a 1.82 ERA in five career appearances at National League ballparks.
away_pitcher_note: Young struggled against the Dodgers on Tuesday, tying a career-high by allowing four solo home runs. In all, the right-hander allowed five runs on six hits over five innings. He was just simply hit hard as he threw just 77 pitches and walked one batter before being removed after the fifth. Young is 3-2 with a 5.50 ERA against the Angels in seven career starts.
summary: 2009-06-14 - San Diego Padres (0) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito gained plenty of experience facing the Angels during his American League career with Oakland (2000-06). He's 12-9 with a 3.55 ERA in 28 starts against them -- his most appearances against any club except Texas (30). In fact, Zito made his Major League debut against the Angels on July 22, 2000. He allowed one run in five innings and earned the decision in a 10-3 A's victory. Zito entered his most recent start last Wednesday at Arizona having received the lowest run support among National League starters, but the Giants supplied him with a veritable cornucopia of runs -- five -- in a 5-4 victory.
away_pitcher_note: After three consecutive solid outings, Lackey took a backward step against the Rays on Wednesday under the big top in Florida. He made it through five innings and 98 pitches, yielding 11 hits and two walks for nine runs (eight earned) while striking out two men. One of the runs scored on a wild pitch, indicative of Lackey's problems finding the strike zone (only 58 times). Lackey, who thoroughly enjoys Interleague Play, has faced the Giants once in the regular season, taking a loss even though he allowed only one earned run in seven innings in San Francisco.
summary: 2009-06-15 - Los Angeles Angels (9) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez walked a career-high seven in his most recent start on Thursday at Arizona. Yet none of those batters scored and he allowed just one run in 5 2/3 innings on Justin Upton's home run. This reflected Sanchez's ability to recover from adversity, which hasn't always been his strong suit. Sanchez's experience against the Angels has been limited to one relief appearance. He's 2-0 with a 3.04 ERA at home, compared to 0-6, 6.39 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: This will be O'Sullivan's Major League debut. He's a big (6-foot-2, 230 pounds) sinker/slider pitcher with a good changeup. It's all about fastball command with O'Sullivan, who is 5-2 with a 6.02 ERA in 10 starts at Triple-A Salt Lake. A 21-year-old San Diego native who attended Valhalla High School and Grossmont College in El Cajon, outside San Diego, O'Sullivan led the Angels farm system last season with 16 wins. He was a third-round pick in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft.
summary: 2009-06-16 - Los Angeles Angels (8) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has pitched into the seventh inning in five straight starts and, taking no chances Friday, tossed a shutout against the Oakland Athletics. The right-hander whiffed eight A's batters and walked just one. He hasn't lost a decision since April 12. Lincecum has never faced the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim.
away_pitcher_note: Palmer won his last start pitching six innings, giving up 10 hits on three earned runs and improving his record to 6-0 with a 4.11 ERA. With the win he joined Jered Weaver as the only two starters to win their first six decisions as an Angel. His changeup got progressively better throughout the game and his cutter was good, but he struggled a little with his breaking ball. Palmer will face the Giants for the first time in his career after making three starts for the team during the 2008 season.
summary: 2009-06-17 - Los Angeles Angels (4) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Winless in his previous three outings, having yielded 13 earned runs in 18 innings, Saunders was back in All-Star form against the Padres on Saturday night. He came within two outs of a complete game, holding San Diego to one run on eight hits, walking one and striking out five men. He'd issued five walks in six innings in his previous start in Detroit, so his command was back. Saunders is 1-1 in two career outings against the Dodgers with a 2.92 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley allowed three runs -- two earned -- over seven innings against the Rangers on Sunday and earned his ninth win of the season, tying him for the National League lead. He has been a workhorse this season, throwing at least six innings in 13 of 14 starts and lasting at least seven innings in eight starts. Billingsley has allowed fewer than four earned runs in all but one appearance this year. On the road this season, he is 3-1 with a 2.48 ERA in six starts. Billingsley is 1-2 with a 2.45 ERA in five career games -- three starts -- against the Angels.
summary: 2009-06-19 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Turning up the heat in his bid for his first All-Star Game appearance, Weaver is coming off the first complete-game shutout of his career, a dominant five-hit effort against the Padres at home on Sunday.  He walked one man while striking out five. The crossfiring right-hander has yielded just 10 earned runs in his past 89 2/3 innings, yielding one or no runs in six of his past eight starts. Weaver has pitched brilliantly in the past against the Dodgers, going 3-1 with a 1.59 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre hasn't formally announced his decision, but Weaver is expected to make his first start since May 20 because injured starter Eric Stults will not by ready and Eric Milton isn't eligible to come off the disabled list until Sunday. Coincidentally, Weaver would be scheduled to start against his brother, Jered, on Saturday. It will mark the first time the two brothers have pitched against each other.
summary: 2009-06-20 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ending a four-start victory drought, Lackey had a lively fastball and crackling curveball in striking out 10 Giants and walking none in a strong seven-inning effort at AT&T Park on Monday night. Lackey scattered 10 hits and carried a shutout into the sixth, finishing with three earned runs charged to him after throwing 106 pitches, 74 for strikes. One of the most successful pitchers in Interleague history, Lackey has been brilliant against the Dodgers. He's 5-1 in eight starts with a 1.50 ERA in 54 innings against the Angels' turf rivals. He had a no-decision on May 23 at Dodger Stadium, yielding three earned runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw bounced back from his worst start of the season by blanking the A's for 5 2/3 innings on Tuesday. It wasn't pretty as he walked three and needed 105 pitches to get through those 5 2/3 innings, but he did strike out eight batters. It was a marked improvement from his previous start when he lasted just 2 2/3 innings against the Padres. Kershaw is 0-0 with a 1.80 ERA in one career start against the Angels.
summary: 2009-06-21 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ Los Angeles Angels (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Matched against Tim Lincecum, his teammate at Fresno in 2007, Palmer had a solid effort on Wednesday in San Francisco. Lasting 6 1/3 innings, he yielded three earned runs on six hits, walking two -- one intentional -- while striking out five hitters. Palmer maintained his unbeaten record when the Angels rallied in the eighth inning to take the lead against Lincecum. Palmer has excelled at Angel Stadium, going 4-0 in six appearances, five as a starter, with a 3.41 ERA. He lost to the Rockies last year while with the Giants, giving up four earned runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cook went seven innings in his last start and won to tie Jason Jennings for the franchise lead in wins with 58. In the 5-3 victory over the Rays, Cook aggressively stayed in the zone against hitters who were hoping his sinker would dip low for balls, and he used the sinker effectively for grounders. He gave up consecutive homers for Carl Crawford and Evan Longoria on breaking balls, but didn't let anything hurt him for the rest of his time on the mound. Cook won his only career start at Angel Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: With Ervin Santana's right triceps tightness forcing him to the 15-day disabled list, O'Sullivan gets his second Major League start. The Angels are hoping he has the same command and poise he brought to the AT&T Park mound on Tuesday night when he held the Giants to one earned run on five hits and one walk across seven innings, striking out five hitters. He's not overpowering, but O'Sullivan, 21, is effective when he puts his fastball in good spots and keeps hitters off balance with a breaking ball and quality changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA and 23 strikeouts against 12 walks in his last four games. He's done it in myriad ways -- skating through traffic on the bases against the Astros on June 2 but giving up only one run in a no-decision, giving up four early runs but pitching a complete-game victory over the Mariners on June 12, and dominating for eight innings against the Cardinals on June 7 and against the Rays in his last start. He can pitch with his fastball  but also can adjust when hitters are too aggressive.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders fought his control early, walking home a run, and yielded a pair of homers while lasting 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Dodgers on Friday night at home. He was touched for four earned runs on six hits and three walks, striking out four hitters. He has made it into the seventh inning in nine of his 14 starts. Saunders has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis held the Pirates to three runs and forced a whopping 20 groundball outs in a 7-3 victory at Coors Field on Friday night. Marquis actually has had better nights. None of his secondary pitches worked. Of course there is a difference between the lineups of the aggressive, experienced Angels and the less accomplished Pirates. But by being allowed to experiment this spring, rather than being forced into competition for a job, Marquis has learned and is better able to adjust to hitters or his own effectiveness level.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner was a tough-luck loser in his last outing, against the Mariners at Safeco Field. He allowed two runs through six innings and almost escaped a rally in the seventh, but Ichiro Suzuki's chopper up the middle tipped off his glove and bounced into right field. So instead hitting into a rally-killing double play, Suzuki reached and the M's went on to score a pair of runs. It was a much better performance for Buckner, who allowed 14 runs in his previous two starts over a span of 10 2/3 innings. When Buckner is effective he is getting outs early in counts and locating his curve ball. When hitters work him deeper in counts he has a tendency to struggle to find an out pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Facing his older brother, Jeff, for the first time, Weaver had his worst outing of the season, giving up more than four runs for the first time in 14 starts. Lasting 5 1/3 innings, Weaver yielded six earned runs on 10 hits and three walks, striking out four hitters. He had given up six earned runs at home in his previous 53 2/3 innings this season. Weaver retired the first seven men he faced but wasn't the same after Russell Martin homered with one out in the third, suddenly losing his command. Weaver is facing Arizona for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was in position for a much-deserved win in his last start against the Mariners but came up short. The left-hander allowed just one run over seven innings of work but two costly errors in the late innings proved costly. First baseman Tony Clark dropped the ball on a throw from Mark Reynolds in the ninth inning that led to the game-winning run. Davis is seeking his first win since pitching six innings against the Padres on June 5.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey followed a winning, seven-inning effort in San Francisco with eight innings in a home loss to the Dodgers, a team he had dominated in the past with a 5-1 record and 1.50 ERA in 54 innings. He yielded four earned runs, two on a James Loney homer, while getting nicked for nine hits and walking four. He struck out five hitters. Lackey has never faced the D-backs. He's 2-1 with a 6.10 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer pitched a career-high 119 pitches in six innings against the Rangers in his last start, cruising to his third victory in a row. Using a steady dose of fastballs and offspeed pitches, Scherzer was able to keep the Texas hitters off balance. He racked up seven strikeouts in the 8-2 victory and appears to be honing his craft and building arm strength. He is brimming with confidence and continues to develop as a Major League pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: In his 11th start in an Angels uniform, Palmer finally tasted defeat, at the hands of the scorching Rockies on Monday night at home. Palmer lasted 4 2/3 innings, surrendering six earned runs on seven hits and five walks. He struck out five. His previous high in runs allowed was five, and the 4 2/3 innings matched his briefest outing in a starting role. Palmer has never faced Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla is 3-0 with a 2.16 ERA in his last for starts after a 2-1 victory over the Diamondbacks on Wednesday night at Chase Field. He allowed one run on six hits and two walks over seven innings while striking out three and is also 5-1 with a 2.96 ERA in his last eight starts. Padilla is 3-2 with a 5.54 ERA in seven starts at home this season. One of those victories came against the Angels on May 16 when he allowed three runs in eight innings and he is 6-3 with a 4.72 ERA in 13 games, including 12 starts, against the Angels in his career.
away_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan pitched well in his second big league start but was plagued by two problems -- his control and the bat of Rockies shortstop Troy Tulowitzki. O'Sullivan needed 101 pitches to get through five-plus innings and allowed three runs, all coming from two homers by Tulowitzki. O'Sullivan's command was simply off as he walked three batters but he at least kept the Angels in the game as he exited with the team down just one run.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 0-2 with a 4.70 ERA in his Past four starts and has a 3.30 ERA in 12 starts after beginning the season in the bullpen. He is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in eight games, including six starts, at home. Left-handed hitters are hitting .213 off him while right-handers are hitting .256. He threw six scoreless innings in a start against the Angels on May 17 that the Rangers eventuallly won, 3-0, after he left the game. He is 1-3 with a 5.35 ERA in 14 games, including five starts, against the Angels in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was on top of his game against the torrid Rockies on Wednesday night at home, limiting them to one run across six innings on four hits, striking out six with one walk. With dominant efforts in two of his past three outings, Saunders tries to find some success in an Arlington ballpark that has been unkind to him. The stylish southpaw was cuffed around for seven earned runs in 5 1/3 innings in Texas in a May 15 loss that ended his four-game winning streak. Saunders is 0-4 in four starts at the Ballpark in Arlington with a 10.29 ERA -- by far his worst in any park.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood beat San Diego 12-2, on Friday despite having what he called "his worst stuff of the season." He struggled with his fastball command, even though it got better in his final inning, the sixth, as he struck out the side looking. Still, Millwood had a sensational June. He was 4-1 with a 1.30 ERA (5 ER/34 2/3 IP). He had his team-high 12th quality start; he had 11 all last season. In his only start against the Los Angeles Angels this season, he allowed two earned runs on nine hits in six innings as the Rangers held on for a 10-8 victory on May 15.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver moved closer to an All-Star Game nod with another quality start, keeping the D-backs in check (six innings, three earned runs, five strikeouts) after the Angels erupted for an eight-run second inning. Focusing more on throwing strikes than hitting corners, Weaver gave up a pair of homers among four hits, walking four. Two of those walks came in the first inning when he struck out two men to leave the bases loaded. Weaver has pitched effectively throughout his career against the Rangers (2.64 ERA in 10 starts) and at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington (2.18 ERA in five outings) but has little to show for it. He's 2-2 in those 10 starts, 1-2 in Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey was dominant across seven innings against the D-backs on Saturday, yielding an unearned run on five hits and three walks, striking out nine. Holding his stuff to the finish, he recorded punch-outs on six of his final seven outs. Lackey is 6-3 with a 3.46 ERA in 10 career meetings against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: The first inning once again gave Guthrie trouble in his last start. Despite picking up his sixth win of the season, Guthrie allowed three earned runs, two in the first, and walked three batters in the Orioles' 6-3 win. After the first, Guthrie calmed down, however, lasting five innings and registering two strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana was unable to make it through the fifth inning in taking the loss in his most recent effort against the Rays at Tropicana Field, yielding six earned runs on eight hits in 4 2/3 innings. Santana, second in the AL in strikeouts last season and fourth in innings pitched, has worked only 31 1/3 innings in his six starts with 21 strikeouts against 13 walks. His velocity has not been close to the consistent mid-90s of last season, but he was at 91 in a Minor League rehab outing on Sunday night. Santana has struggled at home in three starts (0-1, 14.29 ERA) but is 30-15 in 61 career starts at Angel Stadium with a 3.69 ERA. He's 2-2 with a 4.60 ERA in seven career starts against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched well in place of Koji Uehara his last time out, working into the sixth inning, and he was victimized only by a two-run home run by slugger Adam Dunn. Hernandez has worked into the sixth in all three of his starts and has allowed three earned runs or fewer in two of them. The right-hander has walked three batters or more in two of his three starts but has yet to ring up more than three strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan, a 21-year-old right-hander with command and a heavy sinker, continues to pitch superbly filling a hole in the rotation. His third Major League start was in the opener of a big series in Texas, and he responded with six strong innings marred only by back-to-back homers. He yielded six hits and two walks (one intentional) in six innings, striking out five men. O'Sullivan twice worked out of jams, showing uncommon poise for such an inexperienced pitcher. Matt Palmer, initially ticketed for this start, was moved to the bullpen in Texas and worked two scoreless innings on Wednesday night. The Angels are keeping open their options for the No. 5 rotation spot.
away_pitcher_note: Berken struggled again in his last outing against a powerful Red Sox lineup. The right-hander lasted five innings, giving up eight hits and four earned runs to drop his record to 1-5 this season. Berken did use an effective changeup which allowed him to limit what could have been a much wider margin in the loss, and picked up three strikeouts while walking two batters.

home_pitcher_note: A rough and brief outing at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, where he's 0-5 with an ERA of 11.68, lifted Saunders' ERA from 3.66 to 4.24 on Tuesday night. Saunders yielded a career-high four homers among six hits, coughing up eight earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. He walked five men, three of whom scored. Amazingly, Saunders is 21-5 with a 2.60 on the road in his career outside Arlington. He is 5-0 with a 4.15 ERA in six career starts against the Orioles. He prevailed in Baltimore on April 28, going six innings and yielding four runs, two earned.
away_pitcher_note: In what seems to be a string of disappointing decisions, Hill had his worst outing of the season in his last start on Tuesday against the Red Sox. The left-hander lasted just 3 1/3 innings, giving up nine runs, seven earned, on nine hits. Hill ran into trouble from the beginning, allowing a single and a two-run home run in the first three batters he faced. Hill has now given up at least six earned runs in back-to-back starts.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver gets a chance to improve upon his performance in Texas on Wednesday night when he was reached for seven earned runs on eight hits and one walk in 6 1/3 innings, striking out three hitters. After surrendering a total of 21 earned runs in his first 13 outings, Weaver has given up 16 earned runs in his past three starts. Weaver is 2-2 with a 3.30 ERA in 11 career starts against the Rangers. He's 5-1 at home with a 1.83 ERA, striking out 48 in 59 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood went 6 1/3 innings and allowed four earned runs against the Angels on Wednesday. That snapped a string of six consecutive quality starts and raises his ERA to 1.72 over that stretch with a 4-1 record. Millwood has logged at least six innings for the 16th time in 17 starts this season. Against the Angels this season, he has posted a 4.38 ERA in two starts, both in Arlington. The Rangers are 2-0 in those starts. In eight career starts at Angel Stadium, he is 2-3 with a 3.19 ERA over 53 2/3 innings pitched. Millwood threw 104 on Wednesday, the 15th time he's done so in 17 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey was superb, giving up two earned runs on four hits in eight innings in a win against the Orioles his last time out. He retired the first eight and 12 of the first 13 batters he faced. His seven strikeouts put him within one of tying Mark Langston for fifth place on the Angels' list of all-time strikeout leaders. Scioscia said Lackey's stuff was "the best I have seen in a few years." Lackey is 10-10 with a 5.79 ERA against the Rangers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert, sidelined since the beginning of the season with a strained muscle in the back of his right shoulder, is coming off the disabled list to make his first start of the season. The right-hander had a 2.25 ERA in five games (four starts) during a Minor League rehab assignment. He was 0-1 with a 6.92 ERA in three games against the Angels last season, and he was 2-3 with a 5.63 ERA in six starts for the Rangers last year. Nippert replaces Vicente Padilla, who is sidelined with a sore right shoulder but has not yet been put on the disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: The numbers weren't impressive, but Santana made strides in his return to the mound on Friday at home against the Orioles. He yielded six runs (four earned) in five innings, but there was more life on his fastball than in previous returns from issues involving his right elbow, forearm and triceps. He was in the 93-94 mph range, closer to the 94-96 range he held during his 2008 All-Star season. Now it's a matter of finding his rhythm and command and sustaining his stamina deeper in games. Facing the Rangers for the first time this season, he's 7-5 with a 6.46 ERA in 14 career starts against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla last pitched on June 30 against the Angels and allowed five runs in five-plus innings in a 5-2 loss. He gave up 10 hits. Prior to that he was 3-0 with a 2.16 ERA in four starts. He was pushed back four days in the rotation because of some inflammation in his right shoulder but threw in the bullpen on Monday without problem. He is 6-4 with a 4.98 ERA in 14 games, including 13 starts, in his career against the Angels. That's his most victories against any American League team. He is 3-1 with a 3.43 ERA in six starts this season on the road.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Saunders continued to struggle with his command, yielding a leadoff homer to Brian Roberts on a 2-0 pitch en route to yielding six runs (five earned) on seven hits and three walks in 5 1/3 innings. The lefty struck out three hitters. Over his past seven outings, Saunders has seen his ERA rise from 3.26 to 4.44, as the lefty has given up at least four runs on five occasions. Saunders has faced the Yankees three times in his career. He is 1-1 with a 7.63 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Chamberlain had probably the worst start of his young career on Monday, allowing a career-high eight runs in 3 2/3 innings against the Blue Jays. He also tied a career high by surrendering nine hits. Though only three of the runs were earned, there is no doubt Chamberlain struggled, and manager Joe Girardi was frustrated with his right-hander after the game. Chamberlain did not factor into the decision, as the Yankees came back to win, 10-8.
summary: 2009-07-10 - New York Yankees (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Weaver was back in prime-time form, going seven innings against the Rangers and yielding four runs, three earned, while striking out nine at home on Monday night. He overcame a rocky start, giving up two first-inning runs, to settle into a groove, holding Texas to two hits and a walk from the second through the sixth inning. Weaver is 3-1 with a 6.11 ERA in five career starts against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte said he had his best stuff of the season in his last start on Monday, but the results did not show it. The left-hander surrendered six runs in six innings and was plagued by five walks in a loss to the Blue Jays. It has been an inconsistent year for Pettitte, who has looked brilliant at times and struggled at others. One constant: He has had uncharacteristically poor command -- something he is trying to fix moving into the second half.
summary: 2009-07-11 - New York Yankees (8) @ Los Angeles Angels (14) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lackey was cruising with a shutout with two outs in the fifth inning against the Rangers on Tuesday night when everything came apart. Three singles, a double, two walks and a three-run homer by Andruw Jones brought his night to a screeching halt. Lackey yielded six earned runs on nine hits and two walks while striking out six men. away_pitcher_note: Throwing more breaking balls than usual against a familiar foe, Sabathia used the safety of an early lead to pepper the strike zone against the Twins last Tuesday. He allowed just one run and three hits in seven innings, striking out three and walking one -- and all that in the Metrodome, one of his least favorite places to play. Sabathia will move outdoors for his next start, a Sunday afternoon affair in Orange County. He lost to the Angels in his lone start against them this season, allowing four runs in 6 2/3 innings.
summary: 2009-07-12 - New York Yankees (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It was a truly gutsy performance by Braden against Tampa Bay on July 11, having arrived in St. Petersburg late the night before from California as he dealt with his sick grandmother. Pitching with little rest or food over the past week, he battled for six innings and allowed just two runs on five hits to earn his seventh win of the year. And, finally, the offense gave him some support. The 3.47 runs per game in support of Braden are the lowest in the American League. away_pitcher_note: Santana has struggled to recapture his form of 2008 when he was among the AL's most dominant starters, finishing second in strikeouts and fourth in innings pitched. He hasn't made it past five innings in his past three starts, giving up a total of 15 earned runs in 13 2/3 innings. He was touched for five earned runs in four innings on seven hits by the Rangers in his most recent outing on July 8. Santana has dominated the A's in his career. He's 9-1 in 14 games, 13 as a starter, with a 1.36 ERA. He's 4-0 with a 1.50 ERA in six career starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was roughed up for three straight outings heading into the All-Star break. In a 15-3 loss to Cleveland on July 3, the right-hander couldn't throw strikes and, as result, an Indians team that had lost five straight and scored just 13 runs combined in those losses, hit him hard. Cahill pitched 3 2/3 innings, giving up eight runs (five earned) and six hits with two strikeouts and four walks. Against Boston, he allowed four hits and four runs in 5 1/3, while walking three and surrendering two home runs. He has 41 walks in 98 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders showed signs of emerging from a recent funk against the Yankees on July 10 but still gave up five earned runs across five innings, yielding nine hits and two walks while striking out three batters. In his past 14 innings, he has been rocked for 18 earned runs and 22 hits, walking 10 while striking out seven. It has been attributed largely to command flaws, with nothing physically bothering him. He's 7-2 in 11 career starts against the A's with a 3.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro has lost five straight decisions after blanking his first two opponents. A's manager Bob Geren said he liked the way the rookie battled and has seen improvement in his changeup and command. He expects better things to come for Mazzaro in the second half and believes the wins will start to fall in line.
away_pitcher_note: His teammates felt the cross-firing right-hander was worthy of an All-Star spot with his consistently superb work, leading the staff with 120 1/3 innings and 104 strikeouts along with his 10 wins. Weaver has yielded 13 earned runs in his past 18 1/3 innings, his ERA rising from 2.65 to 3.22. He's 2-2 with a 2.56 ERA in seven career outings against the A's and 1-1 in five starts with a 2.48 ERA in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was cruising on July 12 against Tampa Bay until being lifted after four innings for precautionary reasons with lower back stiffness. Anderson has seemingly found his groove recently, allowing just one earned run in his last 18 1/3 innings. He followed up his masterful performance vs. Boston with four shutout innings against Tampa Bay before the back flared up. He'll be one to watch in the second half as he develops confidence and experience in his rookie season.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey headed into the All-Star break on a positive note, delivering one of his finest efforts of the first half against the Yankees on Sunday. Lackey has 43 strikeouts in his past 41 2/3 innings and has made it through at least seven innings in eight of his 12 starts after coming back from a forearm strain that cost him the first five weeks. The Angels are 4-0 in his starts.
summary: 2009-07-21 - Los Angeles Angels (10) @ Kansas City Royals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister pitched five innings and allowed four runs -- two earned -- in his last start, against the Rays. He has also worked into the seventh inning in four of his past seven outings. Bannister last faced the Angels on May 6, 2008. He allowed five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders struggled with the strike zone throughout a loss to the Athletics on Friday night, yielding a career-high six walks in six innings. He surrendered five runs, four earned, with his most errant toss a three-base throwing error on a pickoff attempt that scored the go-ahead run. Saunders also continues to be hurt by the long ball, having given up 22 homers in 118 1/3 innings. summary: 2009-07-22 - Los Angeles Angels (9) @ Kansas City Royals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Weaver lasted only 3 2/3 innings Saturday against the Oakland A's, his shortest outing of the season. He gave up eight hits and five earned runs. Weaver is 10-3 overall with a 3.48 ERA, but he has not been as sharp lately as he was earlier in the season. In his past six starts he is 3-1, but he has a 7.29 ERA during that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Baker delivered a gem of an outing to open the second half. The right-hander held the Rangers to just one run on six hits over eight innings. He kept an aggressive-swinging Texas ballclub off balance by throwing a lot of first-pitch strikes and moving the ball in and out of the strike zone. The Twins hope to see more of that from Baker throughout the second half. He'll next face the Angels, a team he's gone 0-4 against with a 5.88 ERA in six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey delivered nine dominant outings in Oakland on Sunday, holding the A's scoreless on three hits and one walk while striking out six men. Lackey retired Matt Holliday to leave a runner stranded at third in the ninth inning, claiming the win on Bobby Abreu's homer. He has gone at least seven innings in nine of his 13 starts and has been razor sharp in four of his past five, allowing no more than two runs in no fewer than seven innings in those four games. Lackey is 5-5 in 13 career outings against the Twins with a 3.87 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano found the same middle-inning trouble that has plagued him for most of the season in his most recent start against the Rangers. After easing through the first four innings by allowing just one run on two hits, Liriano  faced 11 batters over his final two-plus innings. His performance was much shakier than his line suggests, as he gave up three runs (two earned) on six hits over six-plus innings. Liriano will next face the Angels. In two career appearances against the Angels (one start), Liriano is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer makes his first start since June 28 in Arizona, but he's been keeping busy in the bullpen, having put together a 2.92 ERA in nine appearances. He's 7-1 with a 5.10 ERA in 11 starts. Palmer has been effective at home (4-1, 4.14) and against right-handed hitters, holding them to a .215 batting average and .363 slugging percentage. Left-handed batters are hitting .294 with a .412 slugging mark. Palmer is facing Minnesota for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't exactly the way that Blackburn wanted to start off the second half, as he delivered his worst start since early May. The right-hander lasted just five innings against the A's and gave up seven runs on 13 hits, which tied the most hits allowed by a Twins pitcher this season. Blackburn has been solid with his sinkerball so the Twins hope he can bounce back with the pitch in his next outing. In three career starts vs. the Angels, Blackburn is 0-2 with a 4.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Santana was a little shaky in his last start against the Royals. He last six innings, but allowed five runs on eight hits. He did manage to tie a season-high with seven strikeouts. At times, Santana's breaking pitches looked better than they have all season, but he lacked command and wasn't able to repeat quality pitches. He looked a lot stronger two starts ago on July 16, when he threw eight innings and allowed just one earned run on three hits against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Swarzak gets another go-round in the rotation as Kevin Slowey continues to rehab from his strained right wrist injury. Swarzak certainly earned another start after holding the A's to just two runs on four hits over seven innings in his last outing. While Swarzak was having a hard time locating his fastball early in the outing, he made an adjustment to turn to his curveball and gave up just two hits over his final four innings. Swarzak will face the Angels for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Royals in his last start. It was the fifth start in a row in which Saunders surrendered four or more runs. After a solid start to the season, Saunders has struggled for most of June and July. He's allowed at least four runs in 11 of his 20 starts, and he's currently tied for the American League lead in home runs allowed with 22. That was one positive about his last start against the Royals. He didn't allow a homer after giving up long balls in seven consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start after an 11-day layoff, Pavano started out fine but fizzled in the fifth inning against the Blue Jays on Wednesday. In all, he gave up seven runs on seven hits, four of which were home runs, with two walks and four strikeouts to pick up his eighth loss. The Indians gave Pavano extra time between starts because, in one season with the Indians, he's already approaching the number of innings he pitched in four injury plagued years with the Yankees. Pavano is 2-1 with a 3.98 in three career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver struggled early against the Twins on Thursday, allowing three runs in the first inning but settled down to retire 14 of the next 15 batters he faced with the one runner reaching base on a hit by pitch. Weaver simply battled back from a rough start, tossing seven-plus innings, allowing four runs on six hits while striking out five and walking one. Weaver is 1-1 with a 4.88 ERA in six career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Huff bent but didn't break in a win over the Blue Jays on Thursday. He went 7 2/3 innings -- the second-longest of his 13 Major League starts -- and allowed four runs on eight hits with a walk, four strikeouts and two homers. On the whole, he did a good job keeping the ball down and not letting innings get away from him. Huff is 5-2 over his last nine starts and has shown improvement at this level. This will be the first career appearance against the Angels for the southern California native.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a three-hit shutout of the Athletics in Oakland, Lackey was almost as good in yielding four hits across 7 2/3 innings of a victory over the Twins at home on Friday night. Joe Mauer's two homers were Lackey's only missteps as he kept pounding fastballs and curveballs in good locations, walking two and striking out three men. Lackey has struck out 52 hitters in his past 58 1/3 innings across eight starts, going 5-2. He's 5-5 in 12 career starts against the Indians with a 3.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey is coming off one of his career-best outings, as he found a groove against the Mariners and stayed in it. He allowed just three hits and no runs in seven innings. He threw 26 pitches in the first inning before settling down and retiring 17 of the final 18 batters he faced. He struck out a season-high seven. He is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in two career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Plagued by a fourth inning that saw him give up six runs, Blackburn got the loss, moving his record to 8-5 with a 3.75 ERA. Visibly frustrated with himself after the game, Blackburn said leaving balls up in the zone really hurt him in the fourth after not giving up a hit in the first three innings. Hopefully the righty can have a short memory when he faces the Angels again on July 31st back in Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe a road start will re-ignite Santana, who continues to have problems at home. He fell to 0-4 at Angel Stadium this season with a 12.38 ERA (33 earned runs in 24 innings) when he lasted only 3 2/3 innings and yielded six earned runs against the Twins on Sunday. He's been unable to find a consistent groove or his high-octane fastball after elbow issues delayed his season by six weeks and a forearm strain sent him to the disabled list a second time. Santana is 2-1 with a 3.52 career ERA against the Twins and is 1-0 in two starts at the Metrodome with a 3.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Swarzak once again stopped the Twins' starting pitching woes on Sunday against the Angels, giving up only one earned run is six 2/3 innings to improve to 3-3 with a 3.74 ERA. After Angels hitters picked up his curveball the second time through the lineup, the righty began dominating with his fastball and changeup. Swarzak will have a second go-round at the Angels in Minnesota, hoping to once again dominate.
away_pitcher_note: The Angels are hoping a return to the Metrodome, where he has flourished in the past, and the turn of the calendar will jump-start Saunders, who struggled in July with an ERA of 8.00 in 27 innings. He hasn't won since June 24, against the Rockies, having endured six frustrating outings. His issue has been with fastball command and getting in hitters' counts, walking 15 while notching only 11 strikeouts in those 27 July innings. He's 2-1 with a 3.54 ERA in three career starts against the Twins and 2-0 with a 1.20 ERA in the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Despite some left shoulder tendinitis, Perkins was given the green light to make his last start against the White Sox and the left-hander showed tremendous improvement from his previous outing when he lasted just one inning vs. Oakland. Against Chicago, Perkins allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings. The slider was Perkins' key pitch in the start, with the pitcher saying that he lived and died by the pitch. Next up, he'll face the Angels, a team he's 2-0 against with a 0.56 ERA in two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver's second-half inconsistency is becoming a concern. Fighting his command, he needed 102 pitches to make it through five innings against the Indians on Tuesday night, allowing four earned runs on eight hits and three walks. He has allowed 35 earned runs across his past 45 1/3 innings, covering eight starts, since shutting out the Padres with 119 pitches on June 14. Weaver is 3-2 with a 5.19 ERA in nine road tests and is 2-1 in his career in five starts against the Twins with a 3.12 ERA. At the Metrodome he is 0-1 in two starts with a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In a start when the big right-hander took a few innings to find his rhythm and flow on the mound, Contreras still gave the White Sox a chance to win Wednesday night at the Metrodome. Contreras allowed three runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings, but his five walks (four intentional) drove his pitch count up to 112. Contreras suffered the loss in the finale of Minnesota's three-game sweep, falling to 0-3 with a 5.94 ERA in his three starts since the All-Star break. Contreras has a 5-3 record with a 3.22 ERA lifetime against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Looking the best he has all season, John Lackey won his fourth straight start Wednesday by using all of his pitches effectively,moving his record to 7-4 with a 4.00 ERA. He pitched seven solid innings, surrendering only three hits and one earned run while also striking out eight. The righty finally seems to be hitting mid-season form after sitting out the first part of the season with a forearm injury. Lackey has tossed seven or more innings in 11 of his 15 starts this season including seven of his last eight. In 12 career starts against the White Sox, Lackey is 3-5 with a 4.13 ERA.
summary: 2009-08-04 - Los Angeles Angels (4) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In one of his best outings of the season, Floyd outdueled Yankees pitcher Andy Pettitte, but earned a no-decision in what became a 3-2 White Sox victory on Thursday night. Floyd lasted 7 2/3 innings, allowing one run on four hits while matching a career high with 10 strikeouts. He allowed more than one baserunner in only one inning and threw 63 of his 103 pitches for strikes in producing his 11th quality start in his last 13 outings. Over that span, Floyd is 6-2 with a 2.33 ERA. Floyd also became just the second White Sox pitcher to fan 10 batters this season, that feat last coming on May 9 when John Danks struck out 10 hitters against the Rangers. Lifetime against the Angels, Floyd is 0-2 in three career starts with a 4.12 ERA, but two of his three career complete games have come against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan is coming off a near-perfect game for Triple-A Salt Lake at Sacramento on July 28. He walked the leadoff hitter in the seventh inning on a 3-2 count after having him down 1-2. He threw 122 pitches, 85 for strikes, and about 80 percent of those deliveries were fastballs, according to his catcher, Bobby Wilson. O'Sullivan has been a big shot in the arm for the sagging, injury-riddled rotation, the Angels winning all five of his outings. He keeps his 90-92 mph fastball in good locations and mixes in quality breaking stuff. In 29 innings with the Angels, he has yielded 32 hits and eight walks while striking out 16 hitters.
summary: 2009-08-05 - Los Angeles Angels (2) @ Chicago White Sox (6) (Final)

Over his last four starts, Danks has struck out 15 batters and walked 14. Despite those numbers, however, he is 4-1 with a 3.08 ERA in his last six starts. away_pitcher_note: Santana's struggles continued at the Metrodome on Friday night when he yielded five earned runs on eight hits and two walks in six innings, striking out six. On the positive side, his velocity was consistently in the 91-93 mph range, an upgrade, and he also appeared to have good command of his slider and changeup. He is 2-2 with a 3.99 ERA in four career regular season starts against the Red Sox and pitched twice against them last year. He has pitched twice against them in the playoffs, once in relief last year and in a start in the 2007 ALDS. He allowed two runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The ace turned in another solid season, his fourth with the Red Sox. But October has always been Beckett's favorite time of year. In 2003, he led the Marlins to a World Series championship, firing a shutout in Game 6 at Yankee Stadium. Beckett had a 1.10 ERA in his two World Series starts that year. He was every bit as dominant for the Red Sox in October 2007, going 4-0 with a 1.20 ERA in his four postseason starts. Last year, Beckett was badly hindered by an oblique injury, going 1-0 with an 8.79 ERA in three October starts. But he finishes this season healthy and optimistic. Beckett, however, had an ordinary second half, going 6-3 with a 4.53 ERA in 14 starts. A four-star slump in August brought down his overall numbers. The righty was 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz had been on a roll until his last two starts, when he was rocked for 13 hits and 13 runs over 11 innings. The right-hander turned in a strong September, going 4-1 with a 2.87 ERA in six starts. After spending the first half at Triple-A, Buchholz joined the Red Sox after the All-Star break and took a regular turn in the rotation for the rest of the season. He didn't face the Angels this season but is 1-2 with a 6.35 ERA against them. Buchholz's one win against the Angels came in his first Major League start in Aug., 2007. This season, the right-hander held opponents to a .256 average.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir has made more career starts against the Red Sox than any other club. He is 8-7 with a 3.59 ERA in 23 regular season starts against them.
