home_pitcher_note:
Sabathia will be holding the ball for the first pitch of Game 1 at Yankee Stadium, and while he is aware there are a phone book full of numbers that say the Yankees haven't beaten the Angels much, the left-handed ace can't agree because it's not reality for him.

"Everybody said that we've struggled with them, but this is my first year here, so I don't really know anything about that," Sabathia said.

The Yankees went 5-5 against the Angels this season, including winning three of their last four meetings and securing a series victory at Angel Stadium last month for the first time since 2004. But thus far, the Yankees have done it without a great deal of assistance from Sabathia. He lost both of his starts against the Angels this season, allowing nine earned runs and 17 hits in 13 1/3 innings through outings on May 2 in New York and July 12 in Anaheim.

Yankees manager Joe Girardi said on Tuesday that a key for Sabathia will be keeping the Angels off base and -- once they inevitably do get on -- continuing to attack the hitters.
away_pitcher_note:
Coming out of the chute firing strikes in good locations, Lackey got the Angels rolling against the Red Sox with 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a 5-0 Game 1 AL Division Series victory at Angel Stadium last week.

Getting his first postseason win since Game 7 of the 2002 World Series against the Giants, Lackey yielded four hits and one walk while striking out four batters, outdueling Jon Lester. Lackey had gone 0-3 in six previous postseason starts following his Fall Classic triumph as a rookie.

Lackey has appeared in three playoff games against the Yankees, twice as a starter. He has surrendered three earned runs and 10 hits in 14 1/3 innings for a 1.88 ERA.

The 6-foot-6 tower of strength from Abilene, Tex., worked three shutout innings against New York in the '02 Division Series and had no decisions in two starts in the '05 Division Series.

Lackey won his only start against the Yankees this year, defeating CC Sabathia on July 12 while giving up two earned runs in seven innings. Lackey is 5-7 with a 4.66 ERA in 16 career starts against the Yankees.

Lackey's ability to get movement on his fastball and put it in good locations sets up his big curveball, slider and changeup as complementary deliveries. He'll throw any of his pitches in any counts.
summary: 2009-10-16 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ New York Yankees (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The hoopla concerning Burnett's pairing with backup catcher Jose Molina proved to be all for naught in Game 2 of the ALDS, as Burnett held the Twins to one run on three hits in his first career postseason start. Burnett was effectively wild, issuing five walks and striking out six as he took a no-decision in a game Mark Teixeira won with an 11th inning home run. Burnett was 1-0 with a 4.26 ERA vs. the Angels in 2009, logging a victory on Sept. 23. In the two starts, Burnett allowed six runs on 15 hits in 12 2/3 innings while walking four and striking out 16. He was 5-3 with a 3.51 ERA in 16 starts at Yankee Stadium this season.
away_pitcher_note:
Winning his last seven decisions after a 19-day break in August to mend a knot in his left shoulder, Saunders tied Jered Weaver for the team lead with his 16 wins against seven losses.

Saunders, who allowed two or fewer earned runs in seven of his last eight outings, wasn't needed for Game 4 against the Red Sox in Boston and will be well rested if he draws the assignment at Yankee Stadium. He hasn't pitched since Oct. 4 when he went five innings in Oakland.

The lefty is known as a finesse pitcher but gets his fastball in the 92-94 mph range, to go with a quality breaking ball and changeup. He focuses on early-count outs with his heater.

Saunders, who didn't break into the rotation full time until 2008, consistently has done some of his best work on the road. He's 25-10 with a 3.97 career ERA on the road compared to 23-12 with a 4.43 ERA at home.

Saunders pitched twice at old Yankee Stadium. He beat the Yankees in his sixth Major League start there on Aug. 11, 2006, holding them to three runs -- two earned -- in six innings.

Saunders also worked a scoreless inning in the 2008 All-Star Game at Yankee Stadium.

Owing in part to his roots in Virginia, Saunders has flourished in cool weather. He's 10-1 with a 2.51 ERA in April and 12-4 with a 4.31 in September and October.
summary: 2009-10-17 - Los Angeles Angels (3) @ New York Yankees (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Weaver was in prime form in turning away the Red Sox at Angel Stadium in Game 2 of the ALDS, holding them to two hits and one earned run across 7 1/3 innings in his third career playoff outing and second start.

The two hits, which came in the fourth inning, were the fewert ever yielded in a postseason game by an Angels pitcher who worked at least seven innings.

Weaver was bringing the heat, getting his fastball in the 91-94 mph range, and he put it in all the right places, finishing with seven strikeouts while walking two men.

The cross-firing right-hander has responded all season to the electricity at Angel Stadium. He was 9-3 with a 2.90 ERA in 17 starts at home compared to 7-5, 4.78 on the road in 16 trips to the post.

With increased stamina and strength, Weaver established career highs in innings (211), strikeouts (174), complete games (four) and shutouts (two) while holding hitters to a .246 batting average.

Weaver was 1-1 in three appearances against the Yankees, getting a loss and a no-decision with a 6.08 ERA in two outings at the new Yankee Stadium. He beat the Yanks at home on July 11, giving up four earned runs in six innings.

He's 4-2 with a 5.88 ERA in seven career starts against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte continued to pad his long and illustrious postseason resume with another quality start in Game 3 of the ALDS against the Twins, logging the victory with 6 1/3 innings of one-run, three-hit ball as the Yankees swept Minnesota and advanced to face the Angels. Pettitte walked one and struck out seven in what was the Metrodome's closing act for baseball. Pettitte had some trouble with the Angels in 2009, going 0-2 with a 7.88 ERA in three starts. In 16 innings on May 1, July 11 and Sept. 21, Pettitte allowed 21 hits and 14 runs, walking eight and striking out six. Baseball's all-time leader in postseason innings pitched with 224 2/3, Pettitte is 15-9 with a 3.89 ERA in 36 playoff games and 6-1 with a 3.92 ERA in nine ALCS starts.
summary: 2009-10-19 - New York Yankees (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Kazmir had the least effective of his seven starts with the Angels in Game 3 of the ALDS against the Red Sox on Sunday at Fenway Park, surrendering five earned runs across six innings on five hits and three walks, with one strikeout.

On the plus side, he managed to get through a scoreless sixth inning and get the bullpen lined up for three solid innings while the offense was erupting with late thunder to complete the sweep.

Kazmir, coming to the Angels on Aug. 28 from Tampa Bay in exchange for three prospects, pitched superbly down the stretch. His 2-2 record was not an accurate reflection of his work, the Angels scoring only eight runs while he was on the mound in his six starts. His ERA -- 1.71 in 36 1/3 innings -- is a better indication of how well he pitched.

Kazmir has made four career starts at Angel Stadium, three since joining the Angels, and is looking for his first win in his new home. His ERA is a solid 3.16, and he says he likes the feel of the mound.

The key for Kazmir is getting some bite and good location on his slider, which complements a superb fastball he moves in and out. He also has a plus changeup.

Kazmir is 6-5 in 15 career starts against the Yankees with a sparkling 2.67 ERA across 87 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Joe Girardi announced Sunday that Sabathia would come back to face the Angels on three days rest in Game 4, something he is very familiar with after having done it four times for the Brewers in 2008. Sabathia went 2-1 with a 0.83 ERA in his final three regular season starts as he strapped Milwaukee onto his back, but he ran out of gas in the fourth straight start on short rest, hammered by the Phillies for five runs in Game 2 of the NLDS. The benefit would be having a rested Sabathia ready to go on his usual timetable for a potential Game 7 at Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2009-10-20 - New York Yankees (10) @ Los Angeles Angels (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Lackey was outdueled by CC Sabathia in Game 1 at Yankee Stadium, lasting 5 2/3 innings and giving up four runs (two earned) on nine hits and three walks, striking out three hitters. His defense let him down with several misplays, including a pop fly by Hideki Matsui in the first inning that fell in the infield for a gift RBI single. Lackey also threw away a pickoff attempt for an error, leading to an unearned run.

In what could be his final game as the Angels' ace -- he's an impending free agent -- Lackey hopes to revert to his form in Game 1 of the ALDS when he shut out the Red Sox across 7 1/3 innings at home. He allowed four hits and one walk while striking out four, notching his first postseason win since Game 7 of the 2002 World Series against the Giants.

After missing the season's first six weeks with a forearm ailment, Lackey picked up momentum around the All-Star break and finished strong, going 7-4 after the break with a 3.05 ERA. He was 6-5 at home with a 3.86 ERA in 13 starts. For his career, Lackey in the regular season is 5-7 in 16 starts against the Yankees with a 4.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
In his eighth straight game throwing to backup catcher Jose Molina, Burnett pitched quite well against the Angels, allowing two runs over 6 1/3 innings of an eventual no-decision -- a game that the Yankees later won to take a 2-0 lead in the ALCS. But not everything was smooth for Burnett, who allowed one of those runs to score on a wild pitch and nearly did so twice. Walking two batters and hitting another two, Burnett was not able to completely harness his electric stuff. But he gave the Yankees more than enough to stay within striking distance and eventually win the game in the 13th.

Burnett's next assignment will come in Game 5 at Angel Stadium. He started there just once this season, striking out 11 Angels but lasting merely 5 2/3 innings in the game. Regardless, Burnett earned the win in that contest, allowing a total of two runs on seven hits.
summary: 2009-10-22 - New York Yankees (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (7) (Final)

After going 12 days between starts, Saunders pitched superbly in Game 2 of the ALCS at Yankee Stadium. Getting double-play grounders in each of his last three innings, Saunders pitched through the seventh, holding the Yankees to two runs, one on a solo homer by Derek Jeter.

It was only his second postseason start, but Saunders had the composure of a man who'd been doing it for years. He struck out Mark Teixeira to close a perfect first inning and put away Melky Cabrera after Robinson Cano's RBI triple in the second. Saunders induced double-play grounders from Jeter in the fifth, Hideki Matsui in the sixth and Cano in the seventh.

Yielding six hits and one walk, Saunders struck out five men. He's known as a finesse lefty, but it's something of a misnomer. Fully recovered from a shoulder issue that bothered him off and on most of the season, he can pound 92-94 mph fastballs on the fists or elevate and get hitters to chase with two strikes. He also has a quality breaking ball and changeup that he'll throw in any count.

Combined with his excellent stuff, Saunders has a swagger. He showed it when he pitched a scoreless inning at Yankee Stadium in the 2008 All-Star Game, and he showed it at the new Yankee Stadium while keeping his team in a game it eventually lost with a defensive lapse.
summary: 2009-10-24 - Los Angeles Angels @ New York Yankees (Postponed)

home_pitcher_note: He doesn't throw in the mid-90s, and he doesn't scowl and growl on the mound, creating the image of a fierce competitor. But Weaver's strength -- apart from his cross-firing deception and wide range of pitches -- is his intense ability to focus and perform under duress. His poise and command are what should enable him to settle in as the Angels' ace, replacing good buddy John Lackey. Weaver led the staff in '09 with 33 starts, 16 wins (tying Joe Saunders), 211 innings and 174 strikeouts. In Game 2 of the AL Division Series against the Red Sox at Angel Stadium, he held Boston to a run on two hits across 7 1/3 dominant innings. He's 2-1 with a 2.61 ERA in postseason play, striking out 22 men in 20 2/3 innings with a 1.07 WHIP. His developing two-seam fastball complements his four-seamer, and his changeup and slider are top shelf. Weaver, who lost, 3-2, in the 2008 season opener in Minnesota, is 3-1 with a 3.51 career ERA in six outings against the Twins. He's 27-12 with a 3.27 mark in 53 career starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Baker proved again this spring why he's at the top of the Twins rotation. The right-hander impressed the coaching staff by carrying over some of the changes that he made at the end of last season, particularly his ability to make adjustments within innings. And unlike last spring when he gave up a total of nine homers, he's been able to limit opposing hitters to just one home run through his first 19 1/3 innings of spring. After missing out on his Opening Day start last year due to right-shoulder stiffness, Baker is in line for the honor once again. This time it will come against the defending AL West champion Angels at Angel Stadium. In six career starts in Anaheim, Baker is 0-4 with a 5.88 ERA

home_pitcher_note: An All-Star in 2008, Saunders is hoping to carry his sizzling finish to 2009 into the new season. No pitcher in the game was hotter down the stretch than the lefty from Virginia, who won his last seven decisions in eight starts after spending 19 idle days allowing inflammation in his pitching shoulder to recede. The shoulder had bothered him off and on all season, but he pitched through the pain before finally going to the DL in early August. With Roy Halladay moving to the NL, Saunders has more wins (33) the past two seasons than any AL pitcher, changing speeds effectively behind a low-90s fastball. The Angels' Opening Day starter last year, he shut out the A's over 6 2/3 innings on three hits. He's 3-1 with a 4.10 ERA in four career starts against the Twins and 23-12, 4.43 in 52 outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Despite dealing with some usual spring soreness in his right knee, Blackburn’s spring went about as well as the pitcher could have hoped. Last year, Blackburn was a consistent presence in the rotation – putting together his second straight season with an 11-11 record and nearly identical ERA (4.05 in ’08 and 4.03 in ’09). The Twins rewarded the pitcher with a four-year, $14 million contract this spring – a year before he was arbitration eligible. Now they’ll see if Blackburn can continue to provide them with innings as he’s been right around the 200-inning mark in each of the past two seasons.  But Blackburn has struggled at Angel Stadium, going 0-2 with a 9.72 ERA in two career starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Motivated to return to 2008 All-Star form, when he was one of the AL's dominant starters with 214 strikeouts in 219 innings, Santana had a blip in the spring when he missed a start with an inflamed bursa sac in his right elbow after bumping against a chair. But he came back with lively stuff and is confident his premium mid-90s fastball is back, along with a darting slider and changeup. He lost 3-4 mph off his fastball last season after forearm stiffness cost him the first five weeks, and he returned to the DL. But he put together a strong second half (7-3, 3.90) to salvage the season, delivering at least six innings in 11 of his final 12 starts. He's 2-2 with a 5.13 ERA in seven lifetime outings against the Twins and always has been tough at home: 32-19, 3.74 in 69 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season Pavano's mission was to prove to people that he could still pitch in the Major Leagues. Coming off four injury-plagued seasons with the Yankees, Pavano got an opportunity at a second chance for his career with the Indians. He proved that he can still be a productive veteran by going a combined 14-12 with a 5.10 ERA in 33 starts between the Indians and Twins. Now that he knows he's healthy again, Pavano's goal is to pitch deeper into games and once again reach the 200-inning mark. He'll start off trying to do that by facing the Angels. He's 2-1 with a 5.13 ERA in four career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: New team, new league, same game. Pineiro says he sees no reason why the formula that worked so well for him last season in St. Louis can't continue to create sinking strikes and groundball outs with the Angels. Making his two-seam fastball a major component in his arsenal, along with a quality breaking ball and changeup, Pineiro delivered his best work last year since 2003-04, when he was a combined 30-18 while averaging 203 innings for Seattle. He has evolved from a hard thrower to a location artist. Pineiro struck out 105 while walking only 27 in his career-high 214 innings in 2009. He led the Majors in fewest walks per nine innings (1.14) and highest percentage of ground outs (.641). He is 2-6 with a 4.32 ERA in 14 career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey saw an impressive 2009 season halted by a wrist injury that required season-ending surgery in July. It came after the pitcher delivered 10 wins before the All-Star Game, earning him mention as a possible All-Star selection. But despite coming off wrist surgery, the control pitcher has not shown any signs of it affecting him. The right-hander put up some solid numbers in Grapefruit League play and was pleased by how he was able to command all of his pitches with his surgically repaired wrist. First up will be a start against the Angels. He's 1-0 with a 4.76 ERA in two career starts at Angel Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer, who worked two scorless innings of relief on Tuesday night against the Twins, gets the call with Scott Kazmir on the disabled list for one turn through the rotation, if all goes as planned. Palmer, a journeyman with only three games worth of Major League experience in San Francisco, was a godsend for the Angels last season. Arriving on April 23, Palmer won his first six decisions, the first time in MLB history a rookie at least 30 years old had achieved that feat. Getting movement from his fastball that makes him especially effective against right-handed hitters, Palmer finished 11-2 with a 3.93 ERA in 40 appearances, 13 as a starter. He faced the A's five times without a start or a decision, posting a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who battled all spring for the fifth spot in the rotation, gets his first shot at proving his roster worth Friday when he takes the mound at Angel Stadium, where he owns a 1-0 record and perfect ERA. The lefty is 1-1 with a 2.92 ERA in two career starts against the Angels and is coming off a season during which he compiled a 6-7 mark with an ERA of 5.75. Gonzalez has put much time into improving not only his changeup but his composure as well.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver had a solid season debut on Monday, showing his resolve by preserving a one-run lead by getting out of a bases-loaded jam in the sixth with a fly ball out. His six strikeouts were indicative of quality stuff, his changeup especially effective in concert with his fastball and slider. Weaver allowed five hits and two walks, with 57 of his 94 pitches in the strike zone. He's 3-3 with a splendid 2.71 in 11 career starts against the Athletics and has always been tough at Angel Stadium, where he's 28-12 with a 3.29 career ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets struggled in his first frame in green and gold, giving up two walks and a double en route to throwing 23 of his 94 pitches. His next four innings, though not stellar, went smoother for the righty and gave Sheets confidence heading into his next start. He lasted five innings and gave up three runs on four hits (two earned) while walking four and fanning three in his A's debut. He's faced the Angels just twice in his career, once in 2002 and another time in 2004 when he tossed a one-hit shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders, normally close to unbeatable in April, didn't have it in his season debut against the Twins on Tuesday, yielding five runs in five innings, with three homers among the eight hits he allowed. Saunders wasn't able to put his two-seam fastball where he wanted it, and the Twins pounded him. He was 10-1 with a 2.51 career ERA in April coming in, and he expects to rebound against the Athletics with more aggression and better tempo. He's 9-3 in 14 career starts against the A's, with a 3.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Braden dazzled in his 2010 debut against the Mariners, surrendering one run and four hits while tallying a career-high 10 strikeouts en route to settling for a no-decision in his first start since July 31, 2009. The A's southpaw, who has been forced to pitch with a numb left foot, boasted what Oakland manager Bob Geren deemed one of his best changeups. Also working like clockwork for Braden was his ability to tab first-pitch strikes. In five career starts against the Angels, Braden is 1-3 with a 4.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte draws the honors for the Yankees' home opener, taking the mound after the opening ceremonies and the presentation of the 2009 World Series rings -- appropriate, since Pettitte pitched the clinching game of the Fall Classic against the Phillies. Pettitte accepted a no-decision in the Yankees' 10-inning win over the Red Sox on April 7, holding Boston to one run -- a David Ortiz RBI single -- and six hits over six innings, walking three and striking out four. He also survived a spill when the first batter of the game, Jacoby Ellsbury, collided with him at first base. Pettitte pitched Game 3 and the clinching Game 6 of the American League Championship Series against the Angels last year, faring 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA; he was 0-2 with a 7.88 ERA in three regular season starts vs. the Halos.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was on top of his game early on Wednesday night, carrying a no-hitter into the fourth. But a walk and homer by Justin Morneau jolted him, and he coughed up two more runs in the fifth, one on a J.J. Hardy homer. He struck out four and gave up five hits and a walk in six innings, surrendering four runs. His fastball was consistently in the 92-95 mph range and his changeup was effective, but sliders to Morneau and Hardy beat him. Santana is 5-2 with a 5.21 ERA in eight career starts against the Yankees. This is his first start at new Yankee Stadium. In the old park, he was 2-1, 5.19 in three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez will be looking to make a better impression on the Yankee Stadium crowds than he did in his first start of '10, serving up eight runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Rays at Tropicana Field. Vazquez cruised through the first three frames before his pitches got too much of the plate, with Tampa Bay teeing off -- Carlos Pena and Willy Aybar hit two-run homers and Ben Zobrist added a two-run double. Vazquez has not faced the Angels since 2008, when he was pitching for the White Sox. In his career, Vazquez is 0-1 with a 2.89 ERA in four career starts against the Halos, though he is very familiar with Bobby Abreu -- perhaps too much so. The former Yankee is 20-for-71 (.282) against Vazquez with nine homers and 15 RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro entered the fifth inning of his Angels debut seemingly on top of his game, protecting a one-run lead with ground out after ground out. But he left a few sinkers up in the strike zone, and the Twins hurt him with a Brendan Harris two-run homer. Pineiro departed having yielded three earned runs across six innings. He'll attack the lower part of the strike zone, and the Yankees know it. Pineiro likes to say there are no secrets with his game plan; it's just a matter of execution. Pineiro is 2-0 with a 3.43 ERA in 16 career appearances, eight as a starter, against the Yanks.
summary: 2010-04-14 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ New York Yankees (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hughes will be making his first start of the season after being skipped the first two times through the rotation. After defeating Joba Chamberlain, Alfredo Aceves, Sergio Mitre and the since-released Chad Gaudin in a competition to be the Yankees' fifth starter, Hughes pitched twice in simulated games at the club's Minor League complex in Tampa, Fla., to tune up for this start.
