Hughes is making his second career start vs. the Angels, and his first since 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir makes his season debut after pitching 6 1/3 innings in a California League rehab assignment on Friday night for Class A Rancho Cucamonga against the Dodgers' Inland Empire affiliate. Kazmir, recovered from left shoulder tightness, threw 93 pitches and reached 93 mph with his fastball. He yielded three earned runs on eight hits, all singles, without a walk. He struck out six hitters. Kazmir's command of his slider is key to how deep he can get in games. He hasn't pitched a regular-season game at new Yankee Stadium. He was 1-2 with a 5.04 ERA in five outings in old Yankee Stadium. He's 6-5 with a superb 2.67 ERA in 15 appearances, 14 as a starter, overall against the Yankees, all with Tampa Bay.
summary: 2010-04-15 - Los Angeles Angels (2) @ New York Yankees (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: One is encouraging, but two is a trend. Marcum solidified his status as the Blue Jays' No. 1 starter by throwing another gem against the Orioles on Sunday, going six innings while allowing only two runs. Marcum, often compared to Greg Maddux in terms of pitching style, has an outstanding strikeout-to-walk ratio (11:2) thus far in 2010, which has contributed to his low ERA (3.46) and a minimal WHIP (0.92). He has yet to earn his first win of the season, but Marcum is 2-1 lifetime against the Angels, boasting an impressive 3.04 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver was virtually flawless against the Athletics on Saturday night at home, yielding a solo homer to Kevin Kouzmanoff on a hanging slider in six otherwise dominant innings. He yielded four hits and one walk while striking out seven hitters, reaching 111 pitches, 70 in the strike zone. His fastball command enabled him to throw fewer sliders and changeups than usual. Weaver is 5-1 in six career starts against the Blue Jays with a 3.00 ERA. In his only outing at Rogers Centre, he went seven innings and yielded one run, picking up a win.
summary: 2010-04-16 - Los Angeles Angels (7) @ Toronto Blue Jays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After a fantastic first start resulting in a win over the Rangers, Tallet faltered in Monday's home opener against the White Sox, allowing six runs on eight hits over a six inning span. Andruw Jones in particular had Tallet's number as he homered twice and singled en route to a four-RBI performance. Tallet will look to bounce back against a tough Angels squad this Saturday. He's 0-1 against them with a 7.36 ERA over 11 career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched much better than his linescore would indicate against the A's on Sunday, as the left-hander allowed just one hit through his first six innings and retired 13 batters in a row before things unraveled in the seventh inning. Saunders allowed back-to-back singles and then a ground-rule double to score a run before being removed for Kevin Jepsen, who allowed both runners to score. So Saunders' final line read six-plus innings pitched with four runs allowed on four hits despite pitching so well the first six innings. It won't get any easier for Saunders, who is 1-3 with a 4.68 ERA in five career starts against the Blue Jays.
summary: 2010-04-17 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Toronto Blue Jays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a brilliant one-hit, 12 strikeout performance, spoiled only by a two-run home run by former teammate Alex Rios, Romero will look to carry his success into his start against the Angels on Sunday. Romero has been lights-out in two starts this season, showcasing a 1.80 ERA and a fantastic strikeout-to-walk ratio of 4:1. He has shown improved control from his 2009 rookie campaign that helped contribute to his early successes. In his short history versus the Angels, he is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Santana struggled with his command Tuesday at Yankee Stadium, issuing five walks along with eight hits while surrendering five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. He worked out of trouble on several occasions, relying heavily on his slider to rack up seven strikeouts, but he was hurt by the long ball (two homers) and lack of control, driving his pitch count to 113. Santana has had his problems north of the border -- he's 1-2 with a 7.31 ERA in three career outings at Rogers Centre and is 2-3, 5.97 overall in six starts against the Blue Jays.
summary: 2010-04-18 - Los Angeles Angels (3) @ Toronto Blue Jays (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro followed a so-so debut at home with a brilliant performance on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium, holding the Yanks to one run across seven innings on five hits and no walks while striking out seven, including Alex Rodriguez three times. Pineiro was in command from the outset, retiring 10 of the first 11 men he faced with his two-seam fastball getting exceptional bite, complemented by his changeup and slider. Pineiro has enjoyed success against the Tigers, going 6-2 with a 2.66 ERA in 11 career appearances, nine as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: While the erratically wild Willis form of the past couple years seems to be gone, his pitching remains a work in progress as he tries to build his confidence and, in turn, his velocity. He hit 95 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun in his last outing Tuesday against the Royals, but did it during an opening-inning escape in which he loaded the bases with two walks and a single before holding Kansas City scoreless. He ended up giving up two solo homers and a two-run ground-ball single in his five-inning defeat. His first-inning command will be worth watching as he tries to start in form rather than in search of it.

home_pitcher_note: Wanted: one missing slider. Kazmir couldn't find it Thursday night in New York, throwing only a handful of ineffective breaking balls in a season debut delayed by shoulder stiffness. The Yankees eventually teed off on his fastball and changeup, unloading seven extra-base hits while producing six earned runs in four innings. Kazmir's fastball was in the low 90s -- not as explosive as he'd like, but not bad - and his changeup was inconsistent. He needs all three of his deliveries to be effective.  Kazmir is 2-4 with a 4.69 ERA in eight career outings against the Tigers, and the former Rays ace is looking for his first career win at Angel Stadium. He's 0-2 in four starts with a 3.16 ERA in his new home park.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts into his second season, it's too early to tell whether Porcello is encountering a sophomore slump, but his struggles with hits and pitch counts suggest he's at least in a learning process in how to mesh his sinkerball that served him so well early last season with the power fastball that carried him through the stretch run. Now he'll go up against an opportunistic Angels lineup that can turn little innings into big ones. He had a no-decision in his only start against the Angels last year at Comerica Park, giving up two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver enhanced his credentials as the staff ace with another strong effort in Toronto on Friday night, moving to 24-14 in his career following an Angels loss by holding the Blue Jays to two solo homers across seven innings. Weaver was in command from the start, yielding five hits and walking none while striking out eight hitters. Fastball command is always the key for the cross-firing right-hander, who mixes in a quality slider and changeup. Weaver is 2-2 with a 7.36 in five career starts against the Tigers and is 28-12 with a 3.26 ERA in 55 outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman's last start read almost like two separate outings -- one batter reaching base safely the first time through the Mariners batting order, then only one out the next time through. He finished with 10 runs, eight earned, allowed on nine hits over four innings with four walks and four strikeouts, having used 93 pitches in the process as he tried to recapture the form that allowed him to work so easily through the lineup early. His splitter-slider combination has helped produce a strikeout per inning, but he'd trade some of those for quick outs and less damage. He's 3-3 with a 4.67 ERA in 10 career starts against the Angels, including 7 1/3 quality innings with seven strikeouts during a start in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: On the heels of two disheartening performances, Saunders put it all together in Toronto, throwing strike after strike across eight superb innings. He yielded two unearned runs on five hits and no walks, striking out two men. Pounding the strike zone, the lefty got six first-pitch outs and even threw a strike to second to pick off a baserunner. Saunders is 1-1 with a 5.18 ERA in seven career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is winless through his first three starts for the third consecutive season, and he went through four starts without a win the last couple years. He's hoping he can avoid that fate this time around, and he has the encouragement of his secondary pitches in his favor. He couldn't command his fastball last time out Saturday against the Mariners, but he mixed curveballs and changeups early and often in the counts to hold Seattle to three runs on seven hits over seven innings with six strikeouts and gave the Tigers their deepest outing by a starting pitcher this year. He's 1-2 with a 4.82 ERA for his career against the Angels, the lowest win total he owns against any American League opponent, but over just six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Sunday in Toronto, Santana was back in the All-Star form he showed in 2008, coming within one strike of a shutout before Adam Lind lifted a 3-2 slider into the seats. Santana settled for a 3-1 win, holding the Blue Jays to four hits and no walks while striking out six for his sixth career complete game. Santana felt his changeup was his best pitch, keeping it away from left-handed hitters, and he second-guessed himself for not throwing it to Lind instead of the slider. The Angels have scored only five runs while Santana has been on the mound in his three starts. The Yankees handed him a loss, reaching the righty for five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings on April 13 in New York. Santana is 5-3 with a 5.50 ERA in nine career starts against the Yanks, and he's 32-20, 3.77 in 50 career outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will try for his third straight victory when he takes the ball against the Angels, making his fourth start of the season. The right-hander hurled seven scoreless innings of six-hit ball on Saturday against the Rangers, walking two and striking out seven in a 111-pitch outing. Burnett made two regular-season starts against the Angels in '09, faring 1-0 with a 4.26 ERA. He had a 5.84 ERA in two postseason starts against the Halos in last year's ALCS.
summary: 2010-04-23 - New York Yankees (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander Joel Pineiro continued his impressive start to the season by tossing 7 1/3 scoreless innings to help lead the Angels to a 2-0 win over the Tigers on Monday at Angel Stadium. Pineiro used his sinker to induce eight groundball outs, including a double play, and struck out four while allowing seven hits and no walks. Pineiro is 3-3 with a 3.22 ERA in 17 career appearances, nine starts, against the Yankees. He allowed one run over seven innings in a win against New York on April 14 in his second start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte will try for his third consecutive win when he draws the start against the Angels. The veteran lefty beat the Rangers on Sunday with eight innings of two-run, four-hit ball, striking out four and walking three in a 107-pitch effort. He also defeated the Angels on April 13 in New York, after faring 0-2 with a 7.88 ERA in three regular-season starts last year. He was 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in two ALCS starts last year against the Angels, including winning the clinching Game 6 to send the Yankees to the World Series.
summary: 2010-04-24 - New York Yankees (7) @ Los Angeles Angels (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir earned his first career victory at Angel Stadium by tossing 5 2/3 solid innings against the Tigers on Tuesday. He allowed two runs on six hits while striking out seven batters, throwing five scoreless innings before exiting with two outs in the sixth with runners on second and third. Both both runners scored on a double by Brandon Inge off reliever Jason Bulger. Kazmir is plenty familiar with the Yankees and has a 6-6 record and a 3.14 ERA in 16 outings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez picked up his first victory back with the Yankees on Tuesday, pitching 5 1/3 innings of three-run ball against the A's at the Oakland Coliseum. Vazquez served up two homers while scattering six hits, walking three and striking out six. His velocity remained a concern, relying heavily on off-speed pitches because he has had difficulty controlling his fastball. Vazquez is 0-2 with a 3.51 ERA in five career starts against the Angels, including taking the loss on April 14 vs. the Halos in New York, when he allowed four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings.
summary: 2010-04-25 - New York Yankees (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continued his excellent start to the season with seven strong innings in a no-decision against the Tigers on Wednesday, holding them to two runs on six hits and two walks, striking out six men. Weaver had yielded only one hit and a walk entering the fifth, giving up a solo homer before leaving the bases loaded by striking out Johnny Damon looking. Weaver has had four straight quality starts, walking only five against 27 strikeouts in 26 innings. Weaver is 2-1 with a 4.17 ERA in eight career starts against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Huff went from an incredibly efficient complete game against the Rangers on May 15 to an inefficient, walk-prone start against the Twins on Wednesday. He walked a career-high six batters en route to giving up four runs on three hits in six innings. Such variation from start to start tends to happen for a young hurler like Huff. But he has proven to be capable of pounding both sides of the plate in the past, and it's a matter of doing so with consistency from start to start. He'll be looking for better results in this start near his Southern California roots.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' uneven start to the 2010 season continued when he lasted only 2 2/3 innings against the Tigers on the heels of eight dominant innings in Toronto. Detroit reached the lefty for five earned runs on six hits and two walks, and he registered no strikeouts. Saunders, who gave up four doubles, has yielded 23 hits and six walks in 21 1/3 innings with eight strikeouts. He has fared well against the Indians in five career starts, going 2-0 with a 2.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot wasn't as efficient as he was in his previous start -- a complete-game victory over the White Sox -- but he was very effective in limiting the Twins to an unearned run on two hits with three walks and three strikeouts in a win over the Twins on Thursday. He induced three double-play balls. Talbot has a deep arsenal, including a changeup that can be devastating the second or third time through an opponent's order, because it keeps hitters off-balance. He has been a very effective offseason acquisition for the Tribe thus far.

home_pitcher_note: Santana wasn't as sharp against the Yankees on Friday night at Angel Stadium as he'd been in his previous start when he went the distance in snuffing Toronto, but he kept the Angels in the game and dueled A.J. Burnett on even terms in giving up four earned runs across six innings. Santana's command left him at times -- he hit two batters, one scoring -- but he battled his way through several crises with his premium stuff. Santana is overdue against the Indians. He's 0-6 with a 6.03 ERA against the Tribe in seven career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook was denied his first victory of the season after giving up four runs on eight hits in five-plus innings of work. The righty was pitching to contact in Oakland and the A's finally got to him in the sixth inning. Westbrook was ultimately done in after giving up a two-run homer to Kurt Suzuki in the sixth. Westbrook had command of his fastball and allowed just one walk in the outing, but his inability to put hitters away on two-strike counts caught up with him. He threw 101 pitches in the outing and struck out just one batter. In nine starts against the Angels, Westbrook is 3-5 with a 3.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sophomore slump or not, Porcello has some issues to work out with his mechanics, tweaks to try to put the sink back in his sinker and limit the kind of damage he has experienced in his past few starts. He allowed six runs on 10 hits over four innings last Sunday at Texas, and he has given up 12 runs on 18 hits over 8 1/3 innings in his past two starts. Though some of his pitch selections are up for debate, it's tough to question that his sinker hasn't been as effective this year. Porcello and coaches were looking over video after his last start to determine if he has dropped his arm angle and flattened out his pitches in turn.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers are hoping they have the same success the second time around against Pineiro that the Yankees enjoyed on Saturday. The sinker-ball artist coughed up as many runs (four) in Saturday's first four innings as he had in his first 20 1/3 innings in an Angels uniform, covering three starts. One of those was a blanking of the Tigers through 7 1/3 innings at Angel Stadium on April 19. Pineiro's success hinges on keeping his sinker down in the zone and complementing it with a quality slider and changeup. He's dominated the Tigers in Detroit, going 3-0 in three appearances with a 1.45 ERA. Overall, he's 7-2 in 12 games with a 2.40 ERA against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The main obstacle holding back Bonderman from an encouraging return this year has been the big inning, whether it's in his first inning or his second time through the order. He worked through three solid innings Monday at Texas, protecting a big early lead, but was chased after three hits, a walk and two runs in the sixth. His splitter has become a better pitch than many would have expected, especially potent when paired with a slider that has its old bite back, but it has so far proven difficult for him to find the combination to get through a lineup two or three times without some sort of struggle. He had a quality start against the Angels on April 21 with three runs allowed over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees managed to score four runs against Kazmir with only three hits in 5 1/3 innings on Sunday, aided by four walks and a hit batsman. Kazmir yielded a pair of homers and was down, 3-0, in the second, but he clamped down and left with a lead in the sixth. He appeared to find his absent slider mid-game, mixing it in with his fastball and changeup with his new delivery, in which his hands are held behind his head before uncoiling. Kazmir is 3-4 with a 4.50 ERA in nine career starts against the Tigers, having beaten them on April 20 at home while going 5 2/3 innings. In that start, he allowed six hits and two earned runs, recording seven strikeouts. He's 2-2 with a 3.25 ERA in five career starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: The immediate result from Verlander's last outing was a hard-luck loss Tuesday against the Twins, with two unearned runs allowed, but the long-term result could well be a return to the Verlander domination of last year. A tweak in his mechanics brought better command, plus the finishing pitches that allowed him to rack up seven strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings and hold Justin Morneau and Joe Mauer hitless. Though his pitch count still sits remarkably high -- his 19.4 pitches per innings ranked near the top of AL starters -- he was quietly encouraged. That said, he has topped 120 pitches in each of his past two outings, and he won't have an extra day in between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver turned in his fifth straight quality start when he allowed just one run on seven hits over six innings against the Indians on Monday at Angel Stadium. He didn't have his best command -- he needed 106 pitches to get through six innings --- but still struck out seven batters and walked just one. The right-hander last pitched against the Tigers on April 21, when he allowed just two runs over seven innings but was saddled with a no-decision. He is 2-2 with a 6.34 ERA in six career starts against Detroit and 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in one career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz got the win -- and a save, so to speak -- on Tuesday against the Blue Jays, going a strong eight innings in a 2-1 game and, in the process, giving a depleted bullpen a needed rest. He threw a career-high 117 pitches (80 of them for strikes), allowed seven hits, two walks and a first-inning run and struck out four. Despite the pitch count, he said he still felt strong at the end. Buchholz lost his previous two starts. He allowed three runs on six hits and one walk while striking out 10 in 6 2/3 innings against the Rangers on April 22 when he made 114 pitches. He allowed four unearned runs in a loss to the Rays on April 17 when he pitched five innings, allowing three hits and striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: No longer Mr. April after the worst start of his career, Saunders is hoping a return to the road and Fenway Park, where he has done some of his best work, brings a return to form after two disappointing outings at Angel Stadium. He yielded a total of eight earned runs in 7 2/3 innings in losses to the Tigers and Indians. He was fortunate to hold the Tribe to three runs on nine hits and three walks across five innings on Tuesday night, getting double plays to end three innings. Saunders is 26-10 with a 3.86 career ERA on the road, and he's 3-0, 2.84 in four starts in Boston. He's 4-1, 3.24 overall in eight lifetime outings against the Red Sox.
summary: 2010-05-03 - Los Angeles Angels (8) @ Boston Red Sox (17) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lester struck out 11 and allowed the Blue Jays only one hit -- a leadoff double by Vernon Wells in the second -- in his seven innings to pick up his first victory of the season last Wednesday. He walked leadoff man Mike McCoy twice but picked him off. He made 119 pitches, 75 for strikes, and was able to work both sides of the plate, using a changeup effectively when behind in the count. He regained the feel on his cutter. His curveball was good and he was able to locate his fastball. He was able to keep his pitches down. With all of that going for him, it was the fifth time in his career that he had 11 or more strikeouts in a game.
away_pitcher_note: Santana has good peripheral numbers. They include 28 strikeouts and 10 walks in 33 1/3 innings. He's allowed less than one hit per inning and has a solid 1.23 WHIP for a starting pitcher. But Santana has been hurt by a few mistakes, many of which have ended up a part of the six home runs he has allowed through five starts. He hasn't received a ton of run support and has pitched better than a 1-2 record would indicate. Santana struck out eight in 6 1/3 innings of a no-decision on Tuesday vs. Cleveland.
summary: 2010-05-04 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The big right-hander will renew acquaintances with the Angels, the team he spent his entire career with before signing with Boston as a free agent in December. Lackey recovered from a shaky first inning in his last start to turn in a strong performance at Camden Yards against the Orioles. Over seven innings, he allowed six hits and three runs, two of which were earned. His six strikeouts in that game were a season high. Lackey has given up three earned runs or less in four of his five starts. In his three Fenway starts this season, Lackey is 1-1 with a 6.06 ERA. Opponents are hitting Lackey at a .307 clip so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Like all Angels starters, Pineiro had his ups and downs during April. The biggest downer was Friday's 10-6 loss in which Pineiro wasn't locating his sinker, leading to nine earned runs in 3 1/3 innings. He has walked just five hitters for the year in nearly 30 innings, but the preference is for the hits to innings pitched ratio to fall (40 hits allowed so far). If the control and command are there, Pineiro will be extremely effective. He pitched for Boston on a one-year contract in 2007, going 1-1 with a 5.03 ERA in 31 games exclusively out of the bullpen.
summary: 2010-05-05 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ Boston Red Sox (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka's first start back from the disabled list was a roller-coaster event. He was terrific over his first four innings, giving up just one hit and one run. But in the fifth, the Orioles pounded Matsuzaka for six runs. Overall, he gave up seven hits and seven runs (six earned) over 4 2/3 innings. This will be Matsuzaka's first start of 2010 at Fenway Park. Matsuzaka has made 36 career starts at Fenway, going 19-11 with a 4.37 ERA. He has made just two career regular-season starts against the Angels, going 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA. The win came last year, when Matsuzaka fired six shutout innings. Matsuzaka has limited opponents to a .246 average during his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir continues to make strides toward a return to All-Star form. He pitched effectively in Detroit, holding the Tigers to two runs (one earned) in six innings. He yielded five hits and four walks while striking out seven, bringing his slider into the game along with his fastball and changeup. When he finds his razor-sharp command with all of his pitches, Kazmir will be back in prime form. Kazmir is 8-7 with a 3.59 ERA in 23 career starts against the Red Sox and is 6-4, 3.05 in 13 outings at Fenway Park.
summary: 2010-05-06 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Boston Red Sox (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The staff ace had his franchise record of 18 consecutive quality starts end in his last outing, thanks to a misplay in left field by Milton Bradley and a stiff lower back that contributed to his earliest departure of the season -- one out into the fifth inning against the Rangers on May 1. The discomfort has subsided and Hernandez says he's ready for his seventh start of the season, which comes against the AL West-rival Angels at Safeco Field. Felix has had his way with Angels first baseman Howie Kendrick, who is 2-for-18 with one RBI off Hernandez, while second baseman Kendry Morales is 10-for-28 with one home run and five RBIs against Felix.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver, the new ace of the staff, had his first substandard start of the season in Detroit on Sunday, lasting only 4 2/3 innings and giving up four earned runs on seven hits and one walk, striking out six men. He needed 107 pitches, having thrown 80 after four scoreless rounds before trouble materialized. Weaver is 8-3 with a 4.61 ERA in 14 career starts against Seattle and is 3-3 with a 6.00 ERA in eight outings at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Fister has been the most -- and maybe only -- pleasant surprise for the Mariners. Through five starts, his ERA and WHIP are the best in baseball, feats he has accomplished by leaning on Seattle's solid defense rather than making batters look foolish at the plate. His strikeout rate per nine innings is 4.11. Without dominant stuff, Fister relies on location and by forcing contact. The key is to avoid walks, something he has done well in his past four starts, handing out just two free passes in 31 innings. He's also getting more ground balls than fly balls, a reason why he hasn't allowed a home run yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders' struggles continued with his third consecutive dismal outing, lasting only four innings amid a barrage of Boston hits, including homers by Kevin Youkilis and Bill Hall. Yielding seven earned runs on nine hits and four walks, Saunders was unable to put his pitches in good locations after working a perfect first inning. He'll try to regain command in Seattle's friendly confines, where he is 5-0 in six career starts with a 2.55 ERA. Saunders is 7-1, 3.19 in 10 career outings against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas has made a strong case for why he should stay in the rotation when Erik Bedard returns. After giving up five runs in his first start of the year, Vargas has allowed eight over his next four outings. His formula is along the same lines of Doug Fister's: don't walk batters and let the defense do the talking. But Vargas has shown some bark, too. He struck out a career-high eight batters against Tampa Bay, when he gave up three runs on four hits in 6 2/3 innings. Vargas is pitching consistently, but with an average run support of 3.13, he has been pitching with a slim margin for error.
away_pitcher_note: Santana showed his composure and high-quality stuff in holding the Red Sox to one run across seven innings on Tuesday night at Fenway Park. Boston scored in the first inning but was 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position as Santana struck out seven while allowing seven hits and one walk. He was throwing 93-95 mph with an excellent slider. The Angels have scored only 21 runs in his six starts. Santana is 6-3 with a 4.18 ERA in 15 career starts against the Mariners and is 3-2 with a 4.29 mark in seven starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro rebounded from a pair of subpar outings to deliver a quality start in Boston on Wednesday night, but it wasn't good enough on a night John Lackey tied his former teammates in knots. Pineiro yielded two earned runs across six innings on eight hits and three walks, striking out five men. He delivered 117 pitches, with 73 in the strike zone. Pineiro is 2-4 in 10 career games, nine as a starter, against Tampa Bay with a 5.70 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Garza outdueled Cliff Lee on Wednesday night in Seattle to claim his fifth win of the season. The 26-year-old right-hander allowed two runs on five hits in eight innings, walking one and striking out five. He has pitched eight innings in four of his six starts this season. Garza has the best stuff on the staff, which he can put on display in any given start, and he seems to be maturing on the mound, which has led to his no longer allowing his emotions to get the best of him. Garza is 0-1 with a 6.46 ERA in three career starts against the Angels; he is 0-0 with a 10.80 ERA in one start at Angel Stadium.
summary: 2010-05-10 - Tampa Bay Rays (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir's ERA took a beating on Thursday night at Fenway Park, where the Red Sox collected seven earned runs on six hits and five walks in 4 1/3 innings against the Angels lefty. Kazmir worked out of jams in the first two innings, yielded a two-run homer to Victor Martinez in the third, and then faced six batters, five scoring, in a tough fifth. High pitch counts have been his undoing. He'd thrown 72 pitches through three innings in Boston. Kazmir is facing his former team, the Rays, for the first time since he was traded last August.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann overcame some early control problems Thursday night against the Mariners to pick up his second win of the season. The 6-foot-9 right-hander threw 11 consecutive balls at one point while trying to control his four-seamer that had more movement than normal. Despite the little bump in the road, Niemann held the Mariners scoreless for seven innings on five hits. While getting everything coordinated might be harder for a taller pitcher, the downward angle of Niemann's pitches can make the baseball extremely hard to hit. Niemann is 0-0 with an 8.00 ERA in two career starts against the Angels.
summary: 2010-05-11 - Tampa Bay Rays (7) @ Los Angeles Angels (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continued his solid start to the season by tossing 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a win over the division-rival Mariners on Friday. The right-hander struck out seven batters and allowed just two hits in a dominating performance against Seattle. It was Weaver's sixth quality start in seven outings as he has asserted himself as the ace of the staff this season. He is 3-0 with a 2.77 ERA in four career starts against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky start against Kansas City, Price rebounded with a gem against the A's. He allowed a season-low three hits -- all singles, two of them the infield variety -- and an unearned run over 7 2/3 innings. Price threw 52 pitches in the first two innings against the Royals before settling down. Against Oakland he needed just 58 pitches to get through the first five innings. He struck out six and walked four against the A's. At one point he retired 11 consecutive batters. Price hasn't allowed more than three runs in any of his six starts.
summary: 2010-05-12 - Tampa Bay Rays (4) @ Los Angeles Angels (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has struggled this season but looked better on Saturday against the Mariners when he allowed just one earned run on five hits over 5 2/3 innings against the Mariners. Saunders, though, was still saddled with the no-decision because two unearned runs scored after a throwing error by Kevin Frandsen at third base in the fifth inning. Saunders is 9-4 with a 4.13 ERA in 15 career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Braden will take the mound for the first time since tossing baseball's 19th perfect game on Sunday in a 4-0 A's win over Tampa Bay. In his perfect effort, Braden relied on locating his inside fastball to hitters, which in turn made his changeup more effective. He struck out six Rays and got the rest to either fly out or ground out in ordinary fashion. The last time he faced the Angels, on April 11, Braden earned the win by throwing six innings, allowing three earned runs on five hits while walking one and striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has been a bit inconsistent this season and it showed against the Mariners on Sunday. The right-hander allowed five runs on 10 hits but he did last 6 2/3 innings and struck out five batters. Santana has owned the A's over his career, going 10-2 with a 1.41 ERA against Oakland in 17 career appearances (15 starts).

Pineiro wasn't perfect against the Rays the day after they were on the wrong side of a perfect game against the A's on Sunday, but he was certainly impressive, tossing 6 1/3 scoreless innings on Monday. He allowed just five hits on the night and walked just one while tying a season-high with seven strikeouts. But he was stuck with a no-decision when the bullpen blew a four-run lead. Pineiro is 8-8 with a 4.68 ERA in 22 appearances (17 starts) against the A's in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After stumbling in his season debut on April 30, Cahill has settled down in his past two starts. He's given up a combined three runs (two earned) in those two starts, allowing nine hits and five walks in 10 2/3 innings, while striking out five. Cahill has allowed one home run in that span, after giving up three in his season debut and 27 in 32 starts last year. In three career starts against Los Angeles, Cahill is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA. He is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two career starts at Anaheim.

home_pitcher_note: Holland was 4-1 with a 0.93 ERA in six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City before being called up to replace Matt Harrison in the rotation. He made his first start on Wednesday against Oakland, pitching six scoreless innings in a 10-1 victory. He allowed five hits, walked one and struck out seven. He is now 7-12 with a 5.93 ERA in 22 career starts. He pitched a three-hit shutout against the Angels on Aug, 9, 2009 but lost two September starts against them, leaving him 1-2 with a 4.29 ERA against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note:
Kazmir admitted it was a "little strange" facing his former Rays teammates for the first time on Monday at Angel Stadium but didn't want to use it as an excuse for his command problems after he lasted just five innings and allowed three runs against his former club in a 7-2 loss. He walked three batters, one of which came home to score, and need 107 pitches to get through five innings.
It marked his 12th straight start without pitching past the sixth inning. Kazmir is 6-1 with a 2.05 ERA against the Rangers in 10 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson allowed one run in seven innings in his last start against the Athletics, but left in a 1-1 game and did not get the win. He is still 3-0 with a 1.26 ERA in his last five starts. He has opened the season with seven consecutive quality starts, the first time in club history that's been done. He has an 0.93 ERA in four starts at the Ballpark. Wilson has also not allowed a home run in his last 69 1/3 innings at the Ballpark, which is also a club record. He has a 4.48 ERA in his career against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Three unearned runs, two on passed balls, were Weaver's undoing in a superlative effort against the Rays on Wednesday. The big right-hander had a career-high 12 strikeouts against two walks in seven innings, yielding six hits and two walks while giving up one earned run. Of the 120 pitches he delivered, 80 were in the strike zone. He had great command of his fastball and changeup. It was Weaver's seventh quality start in eight outings. Weaver is 4-3 with a 3.39 ERA in 14 career outings against the Rangers and is 1-3, 3.65 in seven starts in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Danks has made seven starts this season and six have been of the quality variety. In fact, the White Sox most consistent starter gave up three runs to the Twins in Wednesday's 3-2 loss and that effort marked the first time he allowed as many as three runs in a start this season. Danks struck out three, walked three and yielded seven hits over seven innings, including a pair of run-scoring, two-out hits from left-handed hitting Justin Morneau and Denard Span. He threw 109 pitches and 63 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off his second career shutout, a four-hit blanking of the A's in a duel with Dallas Braden at Angel Stadium on Friday night. Saunders was in command from the start, pounding the strike zone with fastballs, curves and changeups while walking two and striking out six hitters. He feels he has regained his aggressive mindset after a run of poor starts, trusting his stuff more and getting ahead of hitters. Saunders has excelled in three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field, where he's 2-0 with a 1.66 ERA and 0.83 WHIP. He's 3-2 overall against the White Sox with a 3.49 ERA in six career outings.
summary: 2010-05-19 - Los Angeles Angels (3) @ Chicago White Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After yielding five runs on four hits in the first inning on April 28 at Texas, Peavy has been dominant. Since then, he has allowed 16 hits and seven runs in 28 2/3 innings, while walking three and striking out 28. Peavy yielded three runs in the first inning in his past outing at Kansas City, but was dominant after that. After surrendering a solo homer to Billy Butler in the third, Peavy gave up only three more hits, all singles. He retired 14 of 15 in one stretch. Peavy has won three straight May starts, after going 0-2 with three no-decisions in his first five starts. He has lowered his 7.85 ERA in April to 5.37.
away_pitcher_note: Santana delivered six solid innings against the Athletics on Saturday, striking out six while yielding three runs (two earned) on seven hits and three walks. He didn't have a crisp fastball early on, but he was getting it up in the 93-94 mph range by the middle innings, and his slider and changeup were effective as well. It was his first win since April 18 when he went the distance in Toronto. Santana is 3-2, 4.88 in nine career games against the White Sox. He's 2-1, 4.79 in four U.S. Cellular Field appearances, three as a starter.
summary: 2010-05-20 - Los Angeles Angels (6) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Very little went right for Penny his last time out. When he made bad pitches, they got hit hard. Even when he made good pitches, he had bad luck. Now he returns home to face his first Major League team, the Marlins. He's 2-1 with a 3.91 ERA in four career starts against Florida. Penny needs to get back to the efficient ways that marked his first seven starts, when he enjoyed quick outs and quick innings. In his loss to the Reds on Sunday, he needed more than 100 pitches to get through five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro returns to Busch Stadium to face his former teammates on the heels of his finest performance with the Angels, a shutout of the Athletics on Sunday at Angel Stadium. Pineiro yielded four hits and a walk, striking out five. Only two A's reached scoring position as Pineiro used his sinker to produce 14 ground-ball outs, needing only 98 pitches to record his sixth career shutout and first with the Angels. Pineiro is 1-1 with a 1.13 ERA and 0.88 WHIP in two career starts against the Cardinals. He's 13-8 with a 3.29 ERA in 29 appearances, 28 as a starter, at Busch Stadium.
summary: 2010-05-21 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Kazmir logged a season-high seven innings Monday night against the Rangers, but lost his third consecutive start, 4-3. With the loss, Kazmir has allowed four or more runs for the fourth time in seven starts this season. So far this season, Kazmir is 0-3 with a 7.59 ERA in road starts. Against the National League, Kazmir owns a lifetime record of 5-3 with a 4.83 ERA in 13 starts. His only other career start against St. Louis came in 2005, when he allowed two runs in four innings and did not earn the decision in a 6-4 loss while with Tampa Bay.
summary: 2010-05-22 - Los Angeles Angels (10) @ St. Louis Cardinals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is coming off his longest start in terms of pitches since 2006, and he's pitching on regular rest. It will be intriguing to see how he fares, though he has said repeatedly this year that he feels stronger than he has in years. After handling Carpenter quite gently last year, the Cardinals seem to be pushing him a little more in 2010. If he responds well on regular rest after 118 pitches, it will be very good news for Carpenter and the team.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver matched his shortest outing of the season Tuesday night against the Rangers, lasting just 4 2/3 innings and picking up a no-decision in an 8-7 loss. He gave up seven runs on seven hits while striking out just one. Weaver is now 1-2 with a 4.56 ERA in his last four starts. He's only made one career start against St. Louis, when he pitched three innings while giving up three runs on five hits on June 10, 2007. He didn't factor into the decision in a 9-6 loss. Weaver is 6-3 with a 3.41 ERA in 11 starts against the National League.
summary: 2010-05-23 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has put together three exceptional starts in the wake of three bad ones, showing that he has regained command and trust in his stuff. He shut down the White Sox on four hits and one earned run on Wednesday night, striking out four while walking two men. He kept his fastball in good locations and kept the ball in the park, never an easy task at U.S. Cellular Field. In those past three starts he has yielded two earned runs across 22 1/3 innings. Saunders shut out the Blue Jays across eight innings in a win at Toronto on April 17 and is 2-3, 3.76 in six career starts against the Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil rebounded from a rough start with a solid performance on the road against the Mariners on Wednesday. The lefty was charged with two runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings, during which he struck out four and walked two en route to a win. In his previous outing, Cecil allowed eight runs in just two innings at home against Texas. Remove that subpar showing against the Rangers and Cecil has fashioned a 2.75 ERA in the month of May. The southpaw has never faced the Angels.
summary: 2010-05-24 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Santana held the White Sox to an unearned run across seven strong innings on Thursday night in Chicago, striking out six while scattering seven hits, all singles, with three walks. Santana's fastball was consistently in the 91-94 mph range, topping out at 96, and he had excellent bite on his slider. He dominated the Jays in Toronto on April 18, going the distance yielding one earned run on four hits while striking out six with no walks. He's 3-3 with a 4.95 ERA in seven career starts against Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Romero continued his strong start to the season on Thursday, turning in a respectable effort on the road against the Mariners. The lefty allowed one run on four hits and ended with five strikeouts and three walks over 6 2/3 innings, but he walked away with a no-decision for his effort. Over his past two starts, Romero has allowed one run over 15 2/3 innings, during which he has piled up 17 strikeouts against four walks. He has gone 2-0 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts in May. In two career starts against the Angels, Romero has gone 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-25 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Los Angeles Angels (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro watched his ERA soar with a performance that mystified him in St. Louis, where he was banged around for nine earned runs on nine hits and three walks in three innings, the big blow a grand slam by rival pitcher Brad Penny. It was all a matter of location, Pineiro unable to find his command of his fastball or slider in the aftermath of his best start of the season, a four-hit shutout against the A's. Pineiro is 2-4 with a 4.55 in 15 appearances, eight as a starter, against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Cito Gaston was quick to point out a positive within Morrow's previous rough start: the pitcher only issued one walk. Morrow has allowed two walks over his past 10 innings after walking 18 in his previous 19 innings for the Jays. Even so, Morrow was not in top form on the road against the D-backs on Friday. The righty allowed six runs on eight hits and finished with five strikeouts over four innings. Morrow has lasted four or fewer frames and allowed six earned runs or more in three of his nine starts this season. In May, he has gone 1-2 with a 9.00 ERA over four starts. In 14 career games against the Angels, Morrow has gone 0-2 with a 4.91 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-26 - Toronto Blue Jays (5) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In a season of experimenting on the fly with his delivery and arm slot, Kazmir appeared to put it all together on Saturday in St. Louis, holding the Cardinals to six baserunners and three hits across seven innings, yielding three earned runs while striking out five. He had good command of his fastball and brought in his slider and changeup with good effect. He isn't throwing as hard as he has in the past, but his fastball has movement and deception. Kazmir is 3-2 with a 2.68 career ERA in eight starts against the Mariners, and he's 2-1, 5.06 in three outings at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lee had a rough go in his last start, but still netted his second win of the season to become the first pitcher in Mariners history to get a victory despite allowing eight runs. It was his worst outing since 2007, and he failed to complete seven innings for the first time this year. Lee said he just didn't have his best stuff, but there's no reason to expect he'll repeat that performance. If anything, it's good he got it out of the way on a night where Seattle's offense actually clicked.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver rebounded from a horrible outing in Texas with a more characteristic performance in St. Louis on Sunday, holding the Cards to three runs (two earned) on five hits and two walks in six innings, striking out eight men. His fastball was razor-sharp and his breaking stuff was hitting the right spots as well. He threw 98 pitches and wanted to go deeper in the game. He was dominant against the Mariners in Seattle on May 7, shutting them out on two hits and three walks across 7 1/3 innings, striking out seven. Weaver is 9-3 with a 4.24 ERA in 15 career outings against the Mariners and is 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA this season at home in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Felix took a step in the right direction during an 8-1 loss to San Diego on Sunday, tossing seven innings and allowing three runs on seven hits. His control was back after a few Jekyll-and-Hyde outings, and he rung up six Padres, but took the loss after getting only one run of support. The King may not be back to quite the level that's expected, but his latest appearance established some much-needed consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was solid against the Blue Jays on Monday at Angel Stadium, allowing three runs on just four hits over 6 1/3 innings. But the Angels offense struggled mightily, recording just two hits on the night in a 6-0 loss. Saunders did struggle with his command, however, as he walked five batters and needed 115 pitches to record 19 outs. Saunders is 7-1 with a 3.06 ERA in 11 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: After a demotion to the bullpen, Snell got a do-over as a starter and made a solid second first impression. He only went five innings because of a predetermined pitch count of around 90 and wasn't very economical, but holding the Padres to one run on five hits certainly counts for something. Especially when the man he replaced, Ryan Rowland-Smith, had been struggling mightily. Snell said he worked the kinks out of his slider while in the bullpen and has restored his confidence in the pitch, giving him more versatility than he had before being demoted.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar has impressive back-to-back victories, one a complete game at Cleveland and the last an eight-inning domination of Texas. Hochevar needed just 107 pitches to go the distance over the Indians and 99 against the Rangers, a game in which he avoided giving a walk for the first time this season. Increasingly, he shows signs of becoming the consistent pitcher that the Royals always envisioned for the nation's No. 1 Draft pick of 2006. He got 11 groundouts and four strikeouts in his last win, indicating his sinker was working well. Hochevar has faced the Angels just once in his career and he took a beating, giving up seven runs in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Santana continued a run of excellent work on Tuesday night at home, going the distance to turn away the Blue Jays with a complete game for the second time this season. Santana's 10 strikeouts were a season high, and while he allowed three homers, all were solo shots. The Jays had only one other hit, Santana complementing his fastball with a sharp slider and changeup. His ERA over his past eight starts is 2.98. He's 3-3, 5.02 in seven career starts against the Royals and is 2-2, 4.60 at Kauffman Stadium.
summary: 2010-05-31 - Los Angeles Angels (7) @ Kansas City Royals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister notched his fourth victory on Thursday at Fenway Park, holding the Red Sox to three runs on nine hits in his six innings. Best of all, he achieved his goal of not walking a single batter. He did give up one home run, although it was a solo shot, and he's surrendered a club-high 10 in his 10 starts. But the Royals' game plan was to get him through six innings and let the pen take over and he delivered that. Bannister has faced the Angels just twice in his career with one loss and a 6.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro was uncharacteristically wild but effective in holding the Blue Jays to three earned runs across six innings on Wednesday at Angel Stadium. Three of his walks came in one inning, along with both Toronto hits, singles, for the three runs. In his five other innings Pineiro allowed one baserunner with a walk, who was quickly erased on a double play. He struck out six, one shy of his season high. Pineiro is 4-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 12 career appearances, eight as a starter, against the Royals. He's 0-2, 10.38 in four games, two as a starter, at Kauffman Stadium.
summary: 2010-06-01 - Los Angeles Angels (3) @ Kansas City Royals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Struggling early against the Red Sox on Friday, Davies was bailed out by a Royals comeback and got his fourth victory despite giving up five runs on seven hits in five innings. He ran up 102 pitches with 60 strikes, but the bullpen also backed him up with four scoreless innings. Despite some command issues, Davies has doled out just four walks in his last four starts after walking 17 in his first six outings. He's pitched well in his two career starts against the Angels with a 1-0 record and a 1.64 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir's up and down season continued with a loss against the Mariners at home on Friday night. Coming off a win and quality effort in St. Louis, he lasted only 5 1/3 innings, yielding six runs (five earned) on eight hits and a walk, striking out only one man for just the second time in his career. He started well, retiring eight of the first nine hitters he faced, but was unable to sustain the momentum generated with back-to-back seven-inning efforts. Kazmir is 2-2 with a 4.89 ERA in eight career starts against the Royals, and he's 0-1 with a 5.40 mark in four outings in Kansas City.
summary: 2010-06-02 - Los Angeles Angels (7) @ Kansas City Royals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Greinke gave up just one run in six innings last Saturday night in Boston, but it was enough to deal him his sixth loss, 1-0. The Royals have rarely supported Greinke offensively this season, averaging just three runs in his 11 starts. Just missing on his location often, he ran up 115 pitches (66 strikes) while giving up five hits and three walks. Afterward, he lamented that his slider, such a good pitch for him last season, was not getting the job done this year, and he's not sure why. Against the Angels last season, he was 0-1 in two starts but had an 0.56 ERA. The loss was 1-0 in a complete-game effort. Next time, he shut them out for eight innings, but the Royals lost, 2-1, in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver pitched brilliantly on Saturday at home against the Mariners, giving up one unearned run across seven innings on three hits and three walks, striking out six. Performing like an ace, Weaver has had good-to-excellent efforts in nine of his 11 outings, pounding the strike zone while getting increasing mileage out of his changeup along with a deadly slider. Weaver is 3-4 with a 3.35 ERA in seven career starts against the Royals and 2-2 with a 5.09 ERA in four outings at Kauffman Stadium.
summary: 2010-06-03 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ Kansas City Royals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Snell lasted just four-plus innings against the Angels on Sunday, allowing three runs on four hits. He had problems with his command, as he walked four batters and needed 82 pitches to record just 12 outs. He'll face the Angels again on Friday and will look to improve on his career 7.04 ERA in three starts against the Halos.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off a rough outing where he ended up with a no-decision last Sunday against the Mariners. The left-hander gave up 10 hits and seven earned runs with three walks as he only last 4 1/3 innings. The Mariners tagged Saunders for six runs in the fourth inning before he was taken out early in the fifth. Saunders will look for his revenge on the Mariners as the Angels open up a three-game series in Seattle.

Santana is rolling as he picked up his fourth consecutive victory against the Royals last Monday. Santana didn't walk a single batter over seven innings, giving up seven hits and one earned run with six strikeouts. He  improved to 4-0 with a 1.86 ERA over his last four starts. The right-hander will look for his sixth victor of the season as the Angels travel to Seattle. In eight career starts at Safeco Field, Santana is 3-3 with a 4.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander had another quality start in his last outing, holding the Twins to six hits and one run over seven innings to join teammate Doug Fister in the under-3.00 ERA club. With four wins, Vargas needs just one more to match his single-season high, set with the Marlins in 2005, when he went 5-5. Vargas has surrendered three or fewer runs in nine of his 10 starts this season. He isn't overpowering, striking out 40 batters in 64 2/3 innings, but keeps balls in the park. Vargas has allowed just six home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro is coming off a complete-game loss to the Royals last Tuesday, where he went eight innings, giving up six earned runs on 10 hits, while striking out two, as the Angels lost 6-3. Pineiro is 1-5 in high last eight starts and his ERA has climbed from 1.77 to 5.16.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old veteran was tagged for a loss in his last start, a 6-4 defeat at Boston on Wednesday. Sheets allowed four earned runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out one. The outing marked the sixth straight start that Sheets had finished at least six innings of work. Sheets faced the Angels once this season, when they touched him up for three earned runs on 10 hits and three walks on April 10. Sheets has fared much better at the Oakland Coliseum this season, as he has a 2.50 home ERA compared to a 7.79 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir is coming off his fourth victory of the season, thanks to stellar run support from the Angels. Before Kazmir took the mound last Wednesday night, he had a three-run cushion, and the Angel sailed to a 7-2 victory over the Royals. Kazmir allowed one run on five hits over 5 1/3 innings, while walking four and striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, A's manager Bob Geren announced Mazzaro will start for Brett Anderson, who landed back on the 15-day disabled list with a strained left forearm. Mazzaro relieved Anderson in the third inning of Thursday's 9-8 win in Boston. Mazzaro gave up three earned runs on nine hits and a walk over 3 1/3 innings while striking out one to earn his first victory of the year.  In two career starts against the Angels, Mazzaro is 0-1 with a 7.88 ERA. He's allowed 11 runs (seven earned) on 17 hits and three walks over eight innings of work in those two starts while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is coming off his fifth victory of the season -- a seven-inning performance against the Royals in which he allowed only four hits and no earned runs to go along with nine strikeouts. As of his last start, Weaver had the best winning percentage for active American League pitchers with a minimum of 50 victories. He holds a .659 (56-29) winning percentage for his career. Weaver has allowed two earned runs or fewer in nine of his past 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Braden is still seeking his first win since tossing baseball's 19th perfect game on May 9. On Friday, he got a no-decision against Minnesota after allowing four earned runs on six hits and one walk while striking out two over 6 1/3 innings. Braden left the mound after allowing four straight batters to reach base in the seventh, giving the Twins a 4-1 lead before they won, 5-4, in 11 innings. In two starts against the Angels this season, Braden is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA. He's thrown 14 innings, allowing seven earned runs on 12 hits and two walks while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: After a terrible start, losing five of his first six starts, Saunders has found his form in winning three of his past four decisions. He kept the ball down and in good spots against the Mariners on Friday night, holding them to one run across six innings with the benefit of three double-play grounders. He scattered eight hits with two walks and one strikeout. Saunders has more wins against the Athletics than any other club, going 10-4 in 16 career outings with a 3.73 ERA. He's 4-1 with a 2.87 ERA in five starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill's streak of winning starts came to a halt on Saturday, as he ended up with a no-decision in a 4-3 loss to the Twins. Cahill had won his previous three starts, but gave up three earned runs on five hits and four walks over six innings Saturday, while striking out six. Still, Cahill is yet to lose in three home starts this season and has a 2.04 ERA in Oakland. Cahill faced the Angels on May 16 in Anaheim, allowing three earned runs on five hits over seven innings, while striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Recapturing his 2008 All-Star form with a brilliant slider to go with superb fastball command, Santana keeps racking up wins while shaving his ERA. He didn't have overpowering stuff in claiming his fifth win in as many outings at Seattle on Saturday, but an offensive eruption gave him a soft cushion for his six innings. He yielded one earned run on seven hits and three walks, striking out two hitters. Santana has ruled the Athletics in his career, going 11-2 with a 1.50 ERA in 16 starts and 18 appearances. He's 5-0 with a 1.38 ERA in nine games and seven starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley let up three earned runs in his last start against the Braves on Saturday, but he was deserving of a better line, tossing a shutout through six innings. He hasn't allowed more than three runs since he gave up four runs on May 5, and his ERA after that game was at 5.06. Now with his ERA at 3.80, and as low as 3.63 two starts ago, it's looking more and more like Billingsley has turned a corner. He has been a considerably better pitcher on the road, where his ERA is 2.78 in six starts, than at home, where his ERA is 4.66 in as many starts. Matt Holliday has a strange career line off Billingsley: five hits - three of which were home runs - four strikeouts, and six walks in 20 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro overcame a rough start to pitch tenaciously through six innings and claim a win on Sunday in Seattle, his former home park. After giving up three first-inning runs, he held the Mariners to one the rest of the way, giving up nine hits and three walks (one intentional) while striking out five men. It was his first win since May 16. Pineiro is 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in three career starts against the Dodgers, and he's 1-0 with a 4.26 ERA in his lone outing at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2010-06-11 - Los Angeles Angels (10) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: He doesn't light up the radar gun or the national consciousness like Stephen Strasburg, but this rookie forced his way into the starting rotation of the team with the best record in the league, so there's something going on here too. Ely is a strike-thrower not afraid of pitching to contact, a rare approach since amateur pitchers have had to adjust to aluminum bats.  And what he lacks in velocity he makes up for in pitching savvy, utilizing four pitches and appreciating the value of pinpoint location. away_pitcher_note: Hentges will look to build on the momentum he created in his first career start against the Cubs. The lefty tossed 4 2/3 scoreless frames with six strikeouts on 84 pitches. He also permitted four walks, but he was able to navigate around them.

home_pitcher_note: Heaney is coming off a rough outing against the Astros, allowing five runs over 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday. He was especially hurt by giving up three home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Everything was working for Plesac through the first seven innings vs. Seattle on Thursday. It wasn't until the eighth that he permitted his first hit. Although he walked three batters and gave up a two-run homer, he proved he's back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani's scheduled start was pushed back a day due to fatigue, but he's coming off one of his best outings in years. He allowed one run over seven innings while striking out 10 against the Astros last Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Civale is coming off his first loss of the year, allowing a season-high five runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings against the Mariners. He also matched another season high by tossing 107 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb will come off the injured list to make his first start since May 4, as he's dealt with a blister. He was solid in his last outing, throwing five scoreless innings against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Thorpe will be added to the roster as the 27th man for the rescheduled doubleheader in Anaheim. He made a spot start against the Angels earlier this season, when he allowed three hits and two runs in four innings ahead of a string of postponements.

home_pitcher_note: Canning has been pitching well in May, posting a 1.59 ERA in three starts. He allowed two runs over six innings at Fenway Park in his last start on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Berríos pitched a season-high seven innings in his Saturday start against the A's, regaining his command after a wild start in Detroit but allowing multiple homers for the first time this season. He leads the Twins with 49 strikeouts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana gets the stating nod in the series opener vs. the A's after allowing three runs in 4 1/3 innings of work on the road against the Red Sox on Sunday. Despite the short outing, Quintana struck out seven and didn't walk any Boston hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Kaprielian, Oakland's No. 10 prospect per MLB Pipeline, allowed one run over five innings against the Red Sox to earn a win in his first Major League start. The Southern California native will be taking the mound near his hometown at Angel Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Sandoval remains in the rotation after allowing two runs over four-plus innings against the Indians on Monday. It'll be his second start of the year after two relief outings.
away_pitcher_note: Bassitt has allowed exactly two runs in six of his last seven outings, posting a 3.43 ERA over that stretch. The right-hander will be making his first start against the Angels this year. In three starts against the Halos last season, he went 1-1 with a 3.52 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bundy has been dealing with a foot issue, but was cleared on Friday for his next start. He has a 10.13 ERA in three starts in May, allowing 15 runs in 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Manaea pitched around heavy traffic on the basepaths to limit the Astros to just three runs on Tuesday, despite allowing 10 hits over six innings. His quality outing kept the A's in striking distance of what was an eventual 6-5 walk-off win over Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Heaney is coming off back-to-back rough outings, allowing 10 runs over his last 8 1/3 innings. He's been hurt by four homers over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Yang will make his third career start when he faces the Angels in Anaheim. Over his previous two starts this season, he gave up three runs over 8 2/3 innings, striking out 10 and walking five. He will be making his second appearance against the Angels after giving up two runs in 4 1/3 innings of relief on April 26.

home_pitcher_note: Canning saw his stretch of three-straight strong starts come to an end against the Twins, allowing four runs over two innings. He gave up a grand slam in the first that spoiled his outing.
away_pitcher_note: Dunning had a strong outing last time out, throwing six shutout innings against the Yankees. In his last start against the Angels, Dunning gave up four runs on six hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bassitt enters Thursday's start on a roll, going 4-0 with a 3.26 ERA over his last eight starts. This will be his second consecutive start against the Angels. He held the Halos to two runs while striking out eight across 7 2/3 innings in a win last Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Shohei Ohtani was originally scheduled to start the game, but was scratched Thursday evening. Sandoval was tabbed to take his place.

home_pitcher_note: Manaea faces the Angels for a second consecutive start. He tossed five innings of one-run ball at Angel Stadium last Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Ohtani saw his scheduled start pushed back a day due to transportation issues to Oakland. His velocity was down against Cleveland his last time out, but he still allowed only two runs over 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Montas had dominant stuff last Monday, but was bit by the home run bug. Despite striking out a season-high 11 batters, he took the loss after allowing two costly homers against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Cobb is coming off a solid outing against the Twins, allowing one run over five innings in the first game of a doubleheader on May 20. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Irvin looks to bounce back after giving up a season-high 10 hits against the Mariners last Tuesday. The left-hander has allowed nine runs on 18 hits in his last two starts after posting a 2.49 ERA over his previous seven.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana was solid against the A's on May 21, but was hurt by two inherited runners scoring. He gave up three runs over 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto gave up four runs over five innings in his last start against the D-backs on Wednesday. He logged a 1.80 ERA in his first three starts of the year, but he's posted a 6.23 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list on May 9.
away_pitcher_note: Bundy has struggled over his last three starts, posting a 15.83 ERA with 17 runs allowed in 9 2/3 innings. He lasted just 2 1/3 innings against the A's last time out.
summary: 2021-05-31 - Los Angeles Angels (1) @ San Francisco Giants (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wood gave up a season-high four runs, including three homers, over six innings against the Dodgers on Thursday. He has a 4.73 ERA in three career appearances against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Heaney has a 7.71 ERA over his last three starts but was better against the Rangers on Tuesday. He went 5 2/3 innings and allowed three runs on four hits in a win.
summary: 2021-06-01 - Los Angeles Angels (8) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Canning is coming off one of his better starts, allowing three runs across six innings with seven strikeouts in a win over the Rangers. The right-hander pitched well against Seattle on May 1, yielding no earned runs across 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheffield didn’t have his best stuff his last time out, but he put the Mariners in position to win by giving up just two runs in five innings against Texas. His best start of the season came against the Halos back on May 2, when he threw six shutout innings of two-hit ball.

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani traded zeros with Oakland's Sean Manaea through five innings in his last start, but he ended up dinged for three runs in six innings in a loss. The two-way star has only made one career start against the Mariners, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dugger is taking the spot of Justin Dunn, who was placed on the IL on Wednesday. Dugger has multi-inning ability, but he’ll only throw two to three innings tops, with Héctor Santiago slated to follow.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb has been phenomenal since returning from the injured list, allowing one run in 12 innings with 12 strikeouts in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning his last time out against Texas, flashing much more intent behind his two-strike pitches than ever before. He’s gone at least six innings in nine of his 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sandoval has fared well in three starts this season, posting a 2.57 ERA with nine strikeouts in 14 innings. He threw five scoreless innings against the A's in his last start on May 27.
away_pitcher_note: Gilbert showed all of his potential in his most recent outing against Oakland, pitching 6 innings that marked his most in a professional game since Aug. 24, 2019, when he was with Double-A Arkansas. He also had an electric fastball that averaged 95 mph and topped out at 98.

home_pitcher_note: Bundy has struggled over his last four starts, posting a 12.33 ERA over 15 1/3 innings. In his last start, he gave up four runs on three homers over 5 2/3 innings in a loss to the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Kowar, ranked as the Royals' No. 4 prospect by MLB Pipeline, will make his Major League debut in the series opener. The right-hander dominated at Triple-A Omaha, going 5-0 with a 0.85 ERA  and 41 strikeouts. He permitted just 10 walks in 31 2/3 innings.
summary: 2021-06-07 - Kansas City Royals (3) @ Los Angeles Angels (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Heaney is coming off a strong start in which he allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings with seven strikeouts against the Giants. It came after he had a 7.71 ERA over his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Bubic allowed four runs (three earned) on eight hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Twins on Thursday, getting into some deeper pitch counts that led to the shorter start. He still logged six strikeouts, though, and his changeup was working well.
summary: 2021-06-08 - Kansas City Royals (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Canning is coming off a rough outing against the Mariners, allowing four runs over 3 1/3 innings. He has an 8.74 ERA over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Keller had some long breaks between innings in the Royals' 14-5 win over the Twins on Friday, but he handled it well. He allowed two runs in five innings to go with five strikeouts and no walks.
summary: 2021-06-09 - Kansas City Royals (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kelly has been a workhorse for the D-backs, having gone at least six innings in five consecutive starts. Since the start of May, Kelly has a 4.36 ERA across 43 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohtani is coming off a strong start against the Mariners, striking out 10 batters without issuing a walk over six innings. He allowed two runs on four hits and picked up his second win.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will be making his third start since rejoining the starting rotation. He opened the year as the No. 3 starter, but he was moved to the bullpen after his first outing. Over his last two starts, he is 0-1 with a 2.70 ERA and 10 strikeouts in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cobb has pitched well over his last four starts, logging a 2.25 ERA and 26 strikeouts in 24 innings. He went seven innings in a win over the Mariners on Saturday, though he was hurt by a grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: Duplantier is making his fourth start of the year for the D-backs. In his previous start on Tuesday against Oakland, he allowed four runs on two hits while walking three over three innings. He has not lasted longer than 4 2/3 innings in any of his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Sandoval has fared well in his four starts this year with a 3.15 ERA and 19 strikeouts in 20 innings. He struck out 10 over six innings against Seattle in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Manaea has totaled a season-high 111 pitches in each of his last two starts. He's been dominant over that stretch, with 15 consecutive scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bundy is coming off his first win of the season, allowing two runs over 5 2/3 innings against the Royals. It came after he had a 9.70 ERA in five May starts.

home_pitcher_note: Montas took a tough-luck loss against the Royals his last time out, looking unhittable through six innings before an unlucky sequence in the seventh that led to three runs scored.
away_pitcher_note: Heaney has been throwing more fastballs and it's paid off with two straight strong starts. He's gone 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA and 14 strikeouts in 13 innings in those two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Irvin has pitched at least six innings in each of his last three starts. His command continues to impress, as he's walked two batters or fewer in each of his 13 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Canning held the Royals to one run over 6 2/3 innings in a win in his last start. He has a 3.86 ERA with 39 strikeouts in 35 innings in his last seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani had a no-decision against the D-backs in his last outing, allowing two runs over five innings with eight strikeouts. He has a 2.67 ERA over his last six starts, with 45 strikeouts in 33 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Manning will be the third of the Tigers’ highly touted pitching prospects to make his MLB debut. The former first-round Draft pick ranks 18th on MLB Pipeline’s Top 100 Prospects list, but he struggled with the home-run ball at Triple-A Toledo until his last start.

Though rotation injuries taxed the Tigers' bullpen last week, another issue was Ureña’s second-inning exit in his last start, allowing eight runs with five hits and three walks against the White Sox on Saturday. He owns a 7.46 ERA in six outings since his last quality start on May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Sandoval is coming off his first career win as a starter, allowing two runs over six innings against the D-backs. He has a 2.77 ERA in five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: The former Royals and Brewers swingman steps into Matthew Boyd’s rotation spot for his first Major League start since May 14, 2017. Peralta posted a 2.75 ERA in six starts for Triple-A Toledo this season, but he topped four innings and 60 pitches only once.

home_pitcher_note: Bundy struggled again on Monday, allowing seven runs over 2 1/3 innings against the A's. He's posted a 9.82 ERA in seven starts dating back to May 2.
away_pitcher_note: Mize has tossed three consecutive quality starts, including 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball for a win at Kansas City on Tuesday. His slider has become an increasingly effective pitch, including a .160 average allowed and 30.9 percent whiff rate.

home_pitcher_note: Heaney has been inconsistent this year and couldn't build off two strong starts his last time out. He gave up three runs over five innings in a loss to the A's on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani earned the win in his last start on Wednesday after holding the D-backs to two runs (one earned) over five innings. He has won each of his last three starts for the Giants, posting a 1.35 ERA over that span.
summary: 2021-06-22 - San Francisco Giants (5) @ Los Angeles Angels (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani has seen his command improve and has a 2.65 ERA with just three walks in 17 innings in June. He allowed one run over six innings in a win over Detroit on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman fired eight innings of two-run ball in his last start against the D-backs on Thursday to lower his ERA to 1.51, the second-lowest mark in the Majors behind only Mets ace Jacob deGrom.
